The Food Safety Officers may require submission of expert reports validating the claimed source of contamination; failure to provide satisfactory proof within a timeframe stipulated by the adjudicating officer shall result in penalties as provided herein.

The Central Pollution Control Board may, subject to conditions as provided herein, grant licenses for the operation of industrial effluent treatment facilities designed to process waste generated under Schedule V industries. Such licenses shall be assignable upon prior written consent of the Board and a demonstration that the assignee possesses equivalent technical expertise and financial solvency to the original licensee. The terms of settlement reached between aggrieved parties concerning remediation obligations arising from past non-compliance with emission standards, as recorded by the jurisdictional State Pollution Control Board, shall be binding on all successors in title to the defaulting industrial unit, provided such recording is acknowledged in any subsequent transfer of ownership or lease agreement. Further, any license granted under this Act may be sublicensed for specific processing activities relating to hazardous waste management, subject to a fee determined by the Board and approval from the relevant State Government.

Where a Public Authority fails to provide information or provides inaccurate information pursuant to a request made under this Act, and such failure or inaccuracy results in demonstrable financial loss to an aggrieved party, that party shall be entitled to seek recovery of dues from the Public Authority. The amount recoverable shall encompass not only the direct pecuniary loss suffered but also reasonable incidental expenses incurred in attempting to obtain the correct information or mitigating the consequences of its absence. Provided that any claim for recovery of dues must be made within a period of three years from the date when the aggrieved party first became aware of the failure or inaccuracy. The Public Authority may, at its discretion, offer alternative redressal measures to avoid formal proceedings aimed at recovery of dues.

An application for a certificate of registration shall be submitted to the State Electricity Regulatory Commission in the prescribed form, accompanied by requisite fees as determined by the regulations framed under this Act. The applicant shall provide detailed particulars regarding the nature of electrical installation proposed, its location, and the anticipated load requirements. Upon receipt of an application, the Commission may direct the applicant to furnish further information or submit clarifications if deemed necessary for a comprehensive assessment. The Commission shall verify the accuracy of the information provided and conduct such inspections as it considers appropriate to ascertain compliance with applicable safety standards and technical regulations. A certificate of registration shall be issued within sixty days from the date of receipt of a complete application, subject to any delays attributable to factors beyond the control of the Commission. Any objection received regarding an applicant’s eligibility may be investigated by the Commission, affording the applicant an opportunity for hearing as provided herein.

Registration of agreements relating to compounding of offences shall be mandatory where such agreement involves a pecuniary consideration exceeding twenty thousand rupees. Every individual or entity entering into an arrangement for the compounding of an offence under this Act shall file a memorandum with the Sub-Registrar having jurisdiction over the place where the offence occurred, within thirty days of the agreement’s execution. The memorandum shall detail the nature of the offence, the parties involved, the amount agreed upon as compensation, and a declaration confirming the voluntary consent of all participants. Failure to register such agreements as provided herein renders the agreement voidable at the option of any party aggrieved. The Sub-Registrar may require further documentation to verify the authenticity of the transaction and shall maintain a record thereof accessible for public inspection subject to applicable privacy regulations.

Where a Public Information Officer fails to respond to a request within the time specified under this Act, or provides an incomplete response, the applicant may serve upon the designated Grievance Redressal Officer a written notice of demand specifying the information not provided and the period within which it is expected to be furnished. Such notice shall clearly state that failure to comply will result in further action as permissible under this Act. The Grievance Redressal Officer, upon receiving a notice of demand, shall immediately investigate the matter and ensure that the Public Information Officer provides the requested information without undue delay. Any applicant aggrieved by non-compliance following such a notice may file an appeal before the Appellate Authority. The authority shall consider all relevant factors and issue directions to rectify the deficiency.

Any authorised officer empowered under this Act to conduct inspections of motor vehicles and related premises shall possess full power of entry, subject to providing reasonable advance notice to the owner or occupier unless exigent circumstances necessitate immediate access. Failure to furnish such notice where reasonably practicable shall render the officer liable for a penalty not exceeding five thousand rupees. Any person obstructing an authorised officer in the exercise of their power of entry, or refusing access when duly requested, shall be deemed guilty of an offence and subject to imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or with a fine as determined by the court. Such obstruction includes concealing vehicles or documents relevant to the inspection.

Any party seeking to introduce evidence demonstrating grounds of revocation of a will under this Act shall be subject to a rigorous burden of proof, requiring presentation of documentary corroboration or testimony from two witnesses of sound mind and understanding who can attest to the testator’s diminished capacity or undue influence at the time of execution. Failure to meet this evidentiary standard shall render such evidence inadmissible. Where revocation is established through fraudulent means, the party responsible shall be liable for damages equivalent to twice the value of the estate distributed under the will, recoverable from both the perpetrator and any legal professional complicit in the fraud. Such recovery may include costs incurred by aggrieved beneficiaries in pursuing legal remedies as provided herein.

An applicant seeking registration of a generating station licence shall submit with the application detailed specifications pertaining to the proposed plant’s electrical infrastructure, including transformer capacity and grid connection protocols. The Central Electricity Regulatory Commission may, upon review of these documents, require submission of an independent verification report from a certified engineer confirming adherence to relevant safety standards. Such reports must be registered with the Commission alongside the initial application. Conditions of licence relating to operational performance shall be determined by the State Electricity Regulatory Commission after consultation with distribution licensees operating within its jurisdiction. The applicant shall also provide proof of financial solvency, demonstrating adequate resources for project completion and ongoing maintenance as provided herein.

Every individual offering a motor vehicle for hire or reward, whether through direct engagement or via an online platform, shall ensure accurate and complete disclosure of all material facts pertaining to the vehicle’s condition, age, registration details, insurance coverage, and any prior history of accidents or repairs. Such duty of disclosure extends to informing prospective passengers regarding limitations on liability as provided herein under this Act. Failure to provide such information, when reasonably requested by a passenger, shall render the operator liable for penalties as determined by the Regional Transport Authority. This obligation applies irrespective of whether the vehicle is operated commercially or privately for reward. The authority may issue guidelines detailing the format and content required for these disclosures, provided that they do not unduly burden operators.

Where an application is received by a Public Information Officer, the Central Information Commission shall determine the appropriate manner of service for providing information to the applicant. The Public Information Officer shall endeavour to provide the requested information within thirty days from the date of receipt of the application, or where the application relates to human rights matters, within seven days. This timeframe may be extended by a period not exceeding fifteen days if the information required involves the consultation with another public authority. Such extension must be accompanied by written notification to the applicant detailing the reasons for delay. The manner of service shall prioritize electronic delivery wherever feasible and where the applicant has indicated a preference for such mode. If electronic delivery is unavailable or refused, the Public Information Officer shall provide the information through postal services registered under the Indian Post Office Act, 1896.

The Central Registering Authority shall maintain a comprehensive register of undertakings operating within territories governed by this Act, accessible for public inspection subject to reasonable restrictions regarding commercially sensitive information. Every undertaking exceeding a specified threshold of annual turnover, as determined by notification in the Official Gazette, is required to submit an initial registration form detailing its principal place of business, nature of operations and list of directors. Subsequent alterations to these particulars shall be promptly reported to the Authority for updating within thirty days. Failure to maintain accurate records or provide timely updates may result in penalties under this Act. The register of undertakings will include a unique identification number assigned upon initial registration, facilitating tracking and verification as provided herein.

Where any food business operator fails to maintain a register of undertakings in the prescribed format, or where the entries within said register are found to be materially inaccurate or incomplete, the licensing officer may issue a notice requiring rectification within thirty days. Any objection to the findings contained in such notice shall be submitted in writing to the State Food Safety Authority, accompanied by supporting documentation. The authority shall consider these objections and provide an opportunity for hearing before rendering a decision, which shall be final subject to appeal under this Act. It is provided that the appellate forum may direct re-inspection of the premises if it deems such action necessary for just determination of the dispute concerning the register of undertakings.

Any licensee operating under a permit issued pursuant to regulations framed under this Act shall adhere strictly to the conditions of licence specified therein; failure to do so constitutes a breach, entitling the licensing authority to initiate proceedings for suspension or revocation. The authority may, prior to any such action, issue a notice requiring rectification of the default within a period not exceeding thirty days. Where the licensee fails to comply with the notice, or where the nature of the breach renders rectification impossible, the authority shall proceed as deemed fit. A party aggrieved by an order suspending or revoking a licence may appeal to the appellate forum established under this Act. The appellate forum’s decision is final, subject to further judicial review on grounds limited to legality and jurisdiction.

Where any individual or organization alleges that activities undertaken by an industrial unit have resulted in environmental degradation exceeding permissible limits as defined under this Act, the burden of proof shall lie upon the complainant to establish, through credible evidence and expert testimony, a causal nexus between the alleged activity and the demonstrable harm. The respondent industrial unit may present counter-evidence to refute such claims, and it shall be incumbent upon the adjudicating authority to meticulously evaluate all submissions. Any determination regarding environmental damage or remediation costs made by the authority is subject to appeal before the appellate tribunal, provided that the appellant demonstrates a clear error of law or fact in the original order. The tribunal may require further investigation as deemed necessary.

For the purposes of this Act, a statutory declaration means a statement of fact made by way of an affidavit or affirmation, sworn or affirmed before a person authorized to administer oaths and affirmations under law, and intended to be used as evidence in legal proceedings or for other official purposes. Such declaration shall be in the form prescribed, or substantially in that form, and may relate to any matter which the declarant is legally obligated to disclose or wishes to assert as true. A statutory declaration presented under this Act shall be deemed admissible as prima facie evidence of the facts stated therein, subject to challenge and proof to the contrary.

Where a Public Information Officer fails to provide information within the time specified under this Act, or provides incomplete or misleading information, an aggrieved person may file a complaint with the designated Grievance Redressal Authority. Such complaints shall be accompanied by a statutory declaration from the complainant, affirming that the information sought falls within the scope of this Act and has not been previously obtained through any other lawful means. The Grievance Redressal Authority shall provide an opportunity for both the complainant and the Public Information Officer to present their case, subject to principles of natural justice. If found to be in violation, the Public Information Officer may face penalties as provided herein. Further, the complainant is entitled to compensation for any demonstrable loss or detriment suffered due to the delay or inaccuracy in information provision.

The license granted to a Public Information Officer under this Act for the provision of information relating to contracts entered into by a public authority shall remain valid subject to adherence to all conditions stipulated therein. Any assignment of rights pertaining to access requests processed by a designated officer requires prior written consent from the Central Information Commission, and such consent may be withheld if deemed contrary to the spirit of transparency mandated herein. Further, the grounds of revocation of a license include, but are not limited to, demonstrable failure to comply with prescribed time limits for responding to information requests, intentional disclosure of confidential data beyond that permitted under this Act, or persistent obstruction of access sought by citizens. The Central Information Commission may also revoke such licenses where it finds evidence of commercial exploitation of information facilitated through the licensed process.

Every operator of a commercial vehicle transporting passengers or goods shall ensure that the manner of service rendered to passengers adheres strictly to the guidelines issued by the Regional Transport Authority. Such guidelines shall detail requirements regarding seating capacity, ventilation standards, and provision of potable water. The operator is obligated to display prominently within the vehicle a notice outlining passenger rights under this Act, including procedures for lodging complaints concerning deficient service. Provided that, any deviation from prescribed standards relating to cleanliness or safety shall render the operator liable to penalties as determined by the Transport Appellate Tribunal. Further, passengers may request immediate cessation of services if conditions demonstrably compromise their well-being, subject to verification by a designated authority.

Every State Government shall maintain a Register of Undertakings operating commercial passenger transport vehicles within its jurisdiction. This register shall contain particulars including, but not limited to, the name of the undertaking, registered address, type of vehicle operated, number of vehicles owned or under lease, and details of insurance coverage as required under this Act. The Regional Transport Authority may require undertakings to submit annual returns updating these particulars; failure to do so will render them liable for penalties as prescribed. Entries in the Register of Undertakings shall be open to public inspection during specified hours, subject to reasonable restrictions imposed by the State Government. Any person aggrieved by an entry or omission from the register may appeal to the Transport Appellate Tribunal. The authority responsible for maintaining the Register of Undertakings shall ensure its accuracy and provide copies upon request, provided that a fee is paid as determined by the government.

Where a consumer alleges deficiency in service or unfair trade practice by a service provider, the aggrieved party may submit a statutory declaration affirming the veracity of their complaint and detailing the specific losses incurred as a direct consequence thereof. Such declarations shall be admissible as evidence under this Act, subject to challenge by the opposite party who may present contradictory documentation or testimony. The adjudicating officer shall consider such declarations alongside all other submitted materials; however, failure to substantiate claims within the declaration through corroborating evidence may result in adverse findings against the complainant. Any appeal from an order based on a statutory declaration shall be entertained only if the appellant demonstrates demonstrable prejudice arising directly from its admission or rejection.

Applications for registration of arbitral awards with the designated appellate tribunal shall be submitted in Form A, available on the website of the Ministry of Law and Justice. Each application must include certified copies of the arbitration agreement, the draft arbitral award, any related correspondence between the parties, and proof of service upon all involved parties. The applicant shall declare under oath that the award is final and binding as per the terms of the underlying contract. Provided that, if a party disputes the enforceability of an award, they may submit supporting documentation demonstrating grounds for challenge under this Act. Failure to provide complete information or fraudulent declarations will render the application liable for rejection by the appellate tribunal. The tribunal may require additional documents or clarifications at any stage during processing.

The power to appoint a competent officer for the purpose of verifying documents submitted as evidence under this Act shall vest with the Registrar appointed under the relevant regulatory authority, subject to appeal to the Appellate Tribunal constituted by notification in the Official Gazette. Such appointment may be made on a contractual basis and the terms thereof, including remuneration and duration, shall be determined by the Registrar. The Registrar may delegate the power of appointment to an officer subordinate to him, provided that such delegation is recorded in writing and published on the authority’s website. Any assignment or transfer of rights pertaining to the duties undertaken by a competent officer appointed under this Act requires prior written consent from the Registrar and shall be registered with them. Failure to obtain such consent renders any purported assignment void.

Where an offence has been committed under this Act or in contravention of any direction issued under it, the Central Government or any officer authorized by it in this behalf, may direct the offender to pay a sum of money as compounding of the offence. Such directions shall be passed only after giving the offender an opportunity of being heard. The amount so directed shall be commensurate with the nature and severity of the offence committed and the damage caused to the environment. Provided that no direction for compounding of offences under this Act shall be passed in respect of offences involving death or injury to persons, or those affecting the security of the State.

Where a dispute arises between an electricity distribution licensee and a consumer regarding billing, service connection, or other matters relating to supply, either party shall have the option of seeking resolution through a mutually agreed upon terms of settlement. The process for establishing such terms of settlement will involve written communication outlining the nature of the grievance and proposed remedies. Upon receipt of this communication, the distribution licensee shall acknowledge it within seven working days and appoint an officer not below the rank of Assistant Engineer to facilitate negotiations. Both parties are obliged to participate in good faith during these discussions. Should a mutually acceptable terms of settlement be reached, it shall be documented in writing, signed by both parties, and filed with the State Commission. Failure to adhere to the agreed terms may result in penalties as determined under this Act.

For the purposes of this Act, an “appointed authority” means an officer designated by the State Government, notified in the Official Gazette, to exercise powers and perform duties relating to the registration of vehicles, issuance of permits, and determination of fitness as provided herein. The appointed authority shall be a person possessing qualifications deemed appropriate by the State Government, typically including experience in transport administration or law. An appointed authority may delegate functions under this Act to subordinate officers, subject to conditions specified by the State Government. Any order passed by an appointed authority is appealable before such appellate authority as may be prescribed.

Any person operating a food business requiring a licence under this Act shall strictly adhere to the conditions of licence stipulated therein. Failure to maintain prescribed hygiene standards, as detailed in the Schedule appended hereto, constitutes a violation and renders the licensee liable to penalties not exceeding fifty thousand rupees for the first offence. Subsequent offences may attract cumulative penalties up to one hundred thousand rupees and suspension of the licence for a period determined by the adjudicating officer. The licensing authority may, subject to due process, revoke a licence if conditions are repeatedly breached or if hazardous food is knowingly produced or handled. Any employee found facilitating such violations shall be deemed an accessory and liable to prosecution under this Act.

Applications for the grant of a retail licence relating to packaged consumer goods shall be submitted to the designated Licensing Authority in the prescribed format, along with requisite documentation establishing the applicant's financial stability and adherence to relevant food safety standards. The Licensing Authority may require verification of premises through inspection prior to processing any such application. Conditions of licence granted under this Act shall include, but not be limited to, requirements for maintaining accurate inventory records, prominently displaying consumer grievance redressal mechanisms, and ensuring compliance with advertising guidelines as provided herein. Any alteration in the nature or scale of operations post-licence issuance necessitates notification to the Licensing Authority and may trigger review of existing conditions of licence.

Where a contract for the provision of intellectual property licensing services has been entered into, the right to revoke such license under this Act shall be subject to the terms stipulated within the contractual agreement itself. Provided that any revocation based on breach of contract relating to assignment of rights arising from said licenses may only occur following written notice specifying the nature of the alleged default and affording a period of ninety days for rectification. Further, where a licensee has sub-licensed intellectual property under conditions expressly permitted by the licensor, such sublicensee’s rights shall not be prejudiced by any revocation initiated by the original contracting parties. The grounds of revocation remain limited to those explicitly defined within the initial agreement or as provided herein concerning material breach and insolvency.

Any industrial unit proposing to undertake remediation of land contaminated by hazardous substances shall submit a detailed Remediation Action Plan to the State Pollution Control Board for approval, outlining specific methodologies, timelines, and anticipated outcomes. The plan must demonstrate adherence to established environmental quality standards and incorporate provisions for ongoing monitoring of soil and groundwater parameters. Upon acceptance of the Remedial Action Plan, the Board may facilitate a process wherein affected parties can enter into terms of settlement regarding responsibility for remediation costs and future liabilities. Such settlements shall be documented and filed with the Board, subject to review and approval ensuring equitable distribution of obligations and compliance with applicable guidelines under this Act.

Every distribution licensee undertaking generation or procurement of electricity shall, subject to the provisions under this Act relating to tariff determination, ensure that all contracts entered into for purchase of power from generating companies comply with the principles of transparency and non-discrimination. Provided that any dispute arising concerning the interpretation or application of such contractual obligations may be referred to the appellate tribunal. The appellate tribunal shall give notice to the parties involved and afford them a reasonable opportunity to present their case, adhering strictly to timelines prescribed by regulations framed under this Act. Further, decisions rendered by the appellate tribunal are appealable before the Supreme Court within sixty days, provided that special leave petition is filed demonstrating substantial injustice.

For the purposes of this Act, “prescribed particulars” with respect to goods or services means information relating to their quality, quantity, purity, standard, grade, size, weight, composition, shelf-life, and any other characteristics that are relevant for consumers to make informed decisions regarding purchase. Such prescribed particulars shall be declared by the supplier in a clear, conspicuous, and easily understandable manner on the product packaging or accompanying documentation, as may be specified under this Act. The Central Authority may issue guidelines detailing the format and content of these prescribed particulars, provided that such guidelines do not contradict any other provisions herein.

Where any amount remains due from a food business operator pursuant to an assessment made under this Act or regulations framed thereunder, the State Food Safety Authority may serve upon that operator a notice demanding payment within a period not exceeding thirty days from the date of service. The notice shall specify the amount due, the basis for its determination, and the consequences of failure to comply with the demand. Upon receipt of written objection from the food business operator disputing the assessment or any portion thereof, the Authority shall refer the matter to a Disputes Resolution Panel constituted as provided herein. The panel’s decision regarding recovery of dues shall be final, subject to appeal before the Food Safety Appellate Tribunal within sixty days.

Where a Public Information Officer has been found to have wilfully obstructed access to information or provided false or misleading information under this Act, the Central Information Commission shall issue notice to the officer concerned, affording them an opportunity of being heard in their defence. The Commission may, after considering the response submitted by the officer and any other relevant material, determine whether grounds of revocation of the officer’s designation as Public Information Officer exist. Such determination shall be based on a finding that the conduct of the officer constitutes a serious dereliction of duty or a deliberate attempt to frustrate the purposes of this Act. The Commission may direct the designated authority to revoke the designation of such an officer, provided that the revocation is accompanied by written justification detailing the specific actions leading to the decision and outlining any remedial measures undertaken prior to the determination.

Every food safety officer appointed under this Act shall, upon receipt of a complaint or information relating to an alleged violation of regulations pertaining to food handling, processing, or distribution, immediately initiate inquiries. Such inquiries shall include examination of relevant records, inspection of premises, and questioning of individuals involved in the production or sale of the food article concerned. The competent officer, after conducting such preliminary investigations, may issue a notice requiring the person against whom action is contemplated to appear before him or her at a specified time and place to present his or her case. Any order passed by the competent officer shall be accompanied by reasons for the decision in writing, and copies thereof shall be served upon all affected parties. Appeals against orders of the competent officer may be made to an appellate authority as provided herein.

Where any public authority fails to provide information requested under this Act within the time limit prescribed, or provides incomplete or inaccurate information, a complaint may be filed with the adjudicating officer appointed by the Central Information Commission. The adjudicating officer shall serve notice upon the concerned public authority and afford it an opportunity to present its defence in writing, subject to limitations on submissions regarding procedural compliance. Any party dissatisfied with the findings of the adjudicating officer may appeal within thirty days to a designated appellate body established under this Act; provided that such appeal must demonstrate demonstrable prejudice arising from the original order. The appellate body shall review the record and issue directions as it deems appropriate for remedial action.

Where an employer fails to remit gratuity amounts due to eligible employees within thirty days from the date on which it becomes payable, the Controlling Authority shall have the power to direct the employer to deposit the said amount into a designated government account. This deposit shall be treated as a security deposit against future compliance with the provisions of this Act. The employer shall provide an undertaking to the Controlling Authority confirming the accuracy of the gratuity liability assessment and acknowledging the purpose of the security deposit. Any shortfall in gratuity payments, determined through audit or employee claims, may be recovered from the aforementioned security deposit. Further, where a security deposit is utilized for recovery of outstanding gratuities, the employer shall replenish the amount within ninety days. Failure to do so will result in further action under this Act.

Where a Motor Vehicle Accident Claim Tribunal has ordered recovery of dues from any person liable for compensation under this Act, the Tribunal shall specify the manner in which such recovery is to be effected. The Tribunal may direct that the amount due be recovered by deduction from the salary or other income of the debtor, subject to limitations prescribed by general or special order issued by the State Government. Provided that where the debtor is a partnership firm, the liability for recovery shall extend to all partners jointly and severally. The Tribunal shall serve notice upon the debtor indicating the amount due and the proposed method of recovery, affording him an opportunity of being heard. Any objection raised by the debtor shall be disposed of expeditiously. The State Government may issue guidelines regarding the assessment of income for purposes of deduction and the prioritisation of claims under this Act. Recovery proceedings initiated under these provisions are deemed to be civil debt due from the debtor.

Every manufacturer, service provider, or seller required to register under this Act shall maintain a Register of Undertakings at its principal place of business, accessible for inspection during working hours. The Register shall contain particulars including the date of registration, nature of goods or services offered, address of registered office, details of any subsequent changes in ownership or management, and a record of all complaints received and their resolution as provided herein. Any alteration to the Register must be authenticated by an officer authorised by the Central Authority. Failure to maintain such a Register, or providing false information therein, shall constitute an offence punishable under this Act. The Central Authority may prescribe guidelines regarding the format and content of the Register of Undertakings. An aggrieved party may apply to the relevant authority for inspection of the Register, subject to payment of prescribed fees.

Where a dispute arises concerning the determination of whether an individual possesses the requisite qualifications to act as a competent officer appointed pursuant to an arbitration agreement, the arbitral tribunal shall first ascertain whether such individual meets the criteria specified within the agreement itself. If the agreement lacks clarity on these qualifications, the tribunal may consider relevant industry standards and professional certifications. Any party alleging that an appointed officer lacks competence may petition the designated judicial authority for a determination; provided that such petition must be filed within thirty days of the appointment. The judicial authority shall grant interim relief restraining the officer from proceeding with arbitration only if it finds prima facie evidence of manifest unsuitability. Costs associated with any such petition shall be determined as deemed just by the judicial authority.

Registration officers shall maintain a designated register for recording details pertaining to transactions involving immovable property where a security deposit is provided as part of the contractual agreement. The register shall include, but not be limited to, the names and addresses of all parties involved, the date of execution of the contract, a concise description of the property subject to the transaction, and the amount of the security deposit held by either party. Upon receipt of documentation evidencing the initial creation of such a security deposit arrangement, the registration officer shall record the particulars in the register as provided herein. Any subsequent modification or release of the security deposit requires notification to the registration office, followed by an updated entry within the designated register. Failure to adhere to these requirements may render the transaction voidable under this Act.

Registration of Consumer Grievance Redressal Forums shall be undertaken through an online portal established by the Central Authority, utilizing a standardized digital form accessible on the said portal. Applicants intending to register a new Forum must provide details including its proposed name, registered address, and a list of designated officers with their contact information. The application shall be accompanied by certified copies of relevant incorporation documents, if applicable, and a declaration affirming adherence to guidelines issued under this Act. Upon receipt of an application, the Central Authority may request additional documentation or clarifications as deemed necessary for verification purposes. The entire process is governed by a summary procedure designed to expedite registration while ensuring due diligence and compliance with prescribed norms. Any objection to a proposed Forum’s registration must be submitted within thirty days of public notice.

Every aggregator of transport services utilizing online platforms shall ensure that all vehicles registered under this Act and listed for hire are maintained in a roadworthy condition, subject to verification by an authorized inspector at intervals not exceeding six months. Where a vehicle is involved in an accident resulting in damage or injury, the aggregator shall be liable to provide immediate notification to the relevant authorities and facilitate the assessment of repair costs. To secure compliance with these provisions, every aggregator shall furnish a security deposit with the State Transport Department, the amount thereof determined by regulations framed under this Act. This security deposit shall be forfeited if any vehicle listed by the aggregator is found operating in violation of safety standards or without valid permits, provided that the aggregator fails to rectify such violations within thirty days of written notification.

Applications for registration of proposed industrial units handling hazardous substances shall be submitted to the State Pollution Control Board in the format specified under this Act, along with a detailed environmental impact assessment report and an emergency response plan approved by the competent authority. The Board may, after due consideration of the application and relevant documentation, grant or refuse registration, providing reasons for its decision in writing. Any party aggrieved by such a decision may prefer an appeal to the appellate tribunal within sixty days from the date of receipt of the order. The appellate tribunal shall consider all submissions made by the appellant and the Board before passing any order. Decisions of the appellate tribunal shall be final subject to further appeals as provided herein.

Where a dispute arises concerning the interpretation of a contract containing an arbitration agreement, the arbitral tribunal shall determine whether the requisite information pertaining to the subject matter of the dispute has been disclosed by each party in accordance with the terms stipulated within that contract. For purposes of this determination, any documents or representations expressly identified as forming part of the contractual relationship are deemed to be essential for establishing compliance. Failure to provide such prescribed particulars, where a condition precedent exists under the agreement, shall render the claimant’s remedies subject to limitation, provided that the defaulting party demonstrates good faith in its attempts to rectify the omission. The tribunal may consider extrinsic evidence only if the contract is ambiguous as to the scope of required disclosures.

Where a consumer alleges deficiency in service or goods supplied by an operator, the burden of proof shall lie upon the complainant to establish the said deficiency before the District Commission or State Commission, as applicable. Provided that, where the operator denies the claim, they may present evidence rebutting the allegations made by the complainant. Any attempt by the operator to shift the burden of proof onto the complainant will be deemed an impediment to the fair administration of justice and shall attract a penalty not exceeding fifty thousand rupees. The Commission may, subject to principles of natural justice, direct the operator to produce relevant records pertaining to the transaction in question. Failure to comply with such direction shall result in presumption against the operator regarding the veracity of the complainant’s claims.

Any person engaged in industrial activity involving the release of pollutants into the environment shall, prior to commencement of operations, submit a statutory declaration to the State Pollution Control Board, detailing measures undertaken to prevent environmental contamination and outlining contingency plans for accidental releases. Failure to provide this declaration, or providing a declaration containing false information, renders such person liable to a penalty not exceeding fifty thousand rupees, and may result in suspension of operational license under this Act. The Board shall have power to conduct inspections to verify compliance with the declared measures; non-compliance discovered during inspection attracts an additional penalty as provided herein. Repeated offences will invite prosecution under relevant sections.

Every seller providing goods or services to a consumer shall furnish a detailed notice of demand in case of any deficiency in service or defect in goods. Such notice shall clearly state the nature of the deficiency or defect, the amount claimed as compensation, and the time within which the complaint must be lodged under this Act. Failure to provide such a notice prior to initiating legal proceedings against the consumer shall render the seller liable to a penalty not exceeding two thousand rupees for the first instance, and five thousand rupees for subsequent instances. The adjudicating officer may order the seller to compensate the complainant for any loss incurred due to the delayed or deficient notice of demand, as provided herein.

Where a consumer has suffered loss or injury due to a deficiency in goods or services, they shall have the right to file a complaint with the appropriate forum as provided herein. The consumer may seek compensation including damages, recovery of costs incurred, and restitution of any undue benefit obtained by the service provider or manufacturer. Subject to the provisions relating to dispute resolution, a complaint regarding a violation of their rights under this Act must be made within two years from the date on which the cause of action arose. Provided that, where the violation is continuous in nature, the period of limitation shall run from the date when the consumer becomes aware or should reasonably have become aware of such violation. This period may be extended by the appropriate forum for reasons to be recorded in writing.

For the purposes of this Act, an appellate tribunal is defined as a body established by notification in the Official Gazette for adjudicating disputes relating to goods or services subject to appeal from orders passed by District Commissions. The appellate tribunal shall consist of a Presiding Officer and such number of other members as the Central Government may deem fit, being persons having experience in law, economics, commerce, technology, consumer affairs, or any other relevant discipline. Decisions of the appellate tribunal shall be binding on the parties to the dispute and may be enforced by order of the District Court under this Act.

Any person found to be obstructing an authorized officer conducting an inspection under this Act shall be liable to imprisonment for a term not exceeding six months, or a fine of ten thousand rupees, or both. The authorized officer may, in the course of any inspection, seize any documents, records, or materials relevant to the matter under investigation, provided that such seizure is conducted in accordance with established procedures and documented meticulously within the accompanying inspection report. Failure to provide access to premises or information as requested by an authorized officer shall be deemed a violation subject to penalties prescribed herein. The inspection report documenting findings and observations shall be submitted promptly to the State Pollution Control Board for further action, including initiation of enforcement proceedings where warranted.

For the purposes of this Act, a “register of undertakings” means a publicly accessible electronic record maintained by the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India, containing particulars of all food businesses registered or licensed under this Act. Such register shall include, but not be limited to, the name and address of the undertaking, the nature of its food business operations as defined herein, the date of registration or licensing, and any conditions imposed upon it. The information contained within the register of undertakings shall be updated periodically, subject to verification by the Authority. Access to the register is open to all persons, provided that personal data elements are handled in accordance with applicable privacy regulations.

For the purposes of contracts for the sale of goods, "prescribed particulars" relating to movable property shall include, but not be limited to, the grade, quality, size, and quantity of the goods. Where a contract stipulates that goods must conform to prescribed particulars, such stipulation shall operate as a condition precedent to the buyer’s obligation to accept delivery and pay for the goods. The seller shall provide documentation verifying compliance with these prescribed particulars at the time of dispatch. Failure to furnish such verification does not preclude a claim by the buyer under this Act, provided that the deficiency is demonstrable. Any dispute regarding whether goods meet the prescribed particulars shall be resolved according to procedures as provided herein.

For the purposes of this Act, “generation licence” means a license authorizing a person to generate electricity, and the conditions of licence pertaining thereto shall include, but not be limited to, adherence to grid codes specified by the Central Transmission Utility, compliance with standards for environmental protection as notified by the concerned regulatory authority, and provision of data relating to generation performance in formats prescribed under this Act. A generation licence may also stipulate requirements concerning transmission connectivity and ancillary services. Further, any modification or amendment to the conditions of a generation licence shall be subject to prior approval from the State Commission, provided that such modifications do not fundamentally alter the scope of electricity generation authorized.

Any manufacturer or service provider who fails to comply with the standards of quality, safety, and performance specified under this Act shall be liable to pay a pecuniary penalty not exceeding two million rupees, recoverable as a civil debt. Where a consumer demonstrates that goods or services were deficient and suffered demonstrable harm as a consequence, compensation for such harm shall include all direct losses incurred. The Central Authority may, suo moto or upon complaint, initiate investigations into alleged violations and issue directions to rectify deficiencies. To expedite resolution of disputes, the adjudication process shall follow a summary procedure, prioritizing swift redressal for consumers. Repeated offenders are subject to enhanced penalties, including suspension of licenses as provided herein.

Where a party has performed a contract wholly or partially, but the performance remains incomplete, and the other party refuses to accept the completed portion, such party shall be entitled to recover from the defaulting party so much of the consideration which is just and equitable, having regard to the nature of the contract, the quantum of work done, and the value thereof. The amount recoverable shall not exceed the total contractual price unless it is demonstrated that the incomplete performance conferred a demonstrable benefit upon the recipient. Registration of any such claim for recovery of dues under this Act shall be deemed conclusive evidence of the terms of the agreement and the extent of work performed, subject to judicial review on grounds of fraud or manifest error.

Where a document purporting to be a certificate of registration issued by the Registrar of Societies is produced, that document shall be admissible as evidence of the incorporation and existence of the society named therein, and of its registered office being at the place stated in the certificate. The Registrar may, upon application made by any person interested, certify whether or not a particular body of persons is registered under this Act. Such certification shall be prima facie evidence of the facts stated therein. Any party seeking to challenge the authenticity or contents of a certificate of registration shall do so by filing an objection before the Court at the earliest opportunity. The Registrar shall maintain a registry containing all certificates of registration issued, and any officer authorised by the Registrar may produce such registry as evidence. This production shall be subject to the provisions relating to confidentiality under this Act.

Every insurer, upon receiving a notice of demand served under this Act by an authorized representative of the Motor Vehicle Accident Claims Tribunal, shall within thirty days remit the amount specified in the notice to the designated account maintained by the Tribunal. Failure to comply with this provision shall render the insurer liable for a penalty equivalent to twice the sum demanded, recoverable from the defaulting insurer as arrears of land revenue. The adjudicating officer may issue warrants for recovery and direct attachment of assets belonging to the insurer to satisfy such demands. Further, any employee directly responsible for the delay in remittance shall be subject to disciplinary action by their employer, without prejudice to civil or criminal proceedings under this Act.

Any person intending to register a food processing unit shall submit an application in Form A to the registering officer, along with requisite documentation including a site plan indicating storage areas and effluent disposal mechanisms. The registering officer may, subject to provisions regarding confidentiality under this Act, grant permission for entry into any premises connected with the proposed unit for the purpose of verification of details provided in the application or assessment of suitability. Such entry shall be accompanied by an authorised representative of the applicant. Prior notice of at least twenty-four hours shall be given, except in cases where there is reasonable suspicion that evidence relevant to the registration process may be concealed or destroyed; and the power of entry is subject to limitations as provided herein regarding disturbance of operations.

Any industrial unit engaged in the processing or handling of hazardous materials shall obtain prior consent from the competent authority before commencing operations. This requirement extends to any expansion or alteration of existing facilities that increases the volume of hazardous substances handled, subject to exemptions notified by the Central Government. The appointed authority, designated under this Act for a specific geographical area, is responsible for verifying compliance with prescribed environmental standards and ensuring adherence to safety protocols as detailed in schedules appended hereto. Failure to comply with conditions stipulated during consent issuance may result in penalties including suspension of operations or revocation of licenses. The appointed authority shall also conduct periodic inspections at reasonable intervals, providing advance notice where practicable, and submit reports to the State Pollution Control Board.

Where gratuity is payable to an employee who has ceased to be in continuous service, the employer shall issue a notice of demand to the employee specifying the amount of gratuity determined to be due and providing details regarding the basis of calculation as provided herein. Such notice shall be sent by registered post with acknowledgment due to the last known address of the employee. The employee shall have a period of thirty days from the date of receipt of the notice of demand within which to acknowledge its correctness or raise any objections thereto in writing. Failure by the employee to respond within this timeframe shall be deemed acceptance of the gratuity amount as stated in the notice. Any objection raised must clearly state the grounds for disagreement and provide supporting documentation where applicable, allowing the employer to review and adjust the calculation if warranted.

The fees payable under this Act for various proceedings before an arbitration tribunal or conciliatory authority shall be determined in accordance with the schedule of fees annexed hereto. This schedule specifies rates applicable to applications, awards, and other submissions presented to the tribunal. The fee for registration of a domestic arbitral agreement shall be as prescribed within the schedule. Provided that where a party is demonstrably unable to pay the prescribed fee due to financial hardship, the authority may waive or reduce such fee subject to guidelines issued by the Central Government. Any amendments to this schedule of fees shall be made through notification in the Official Gazette.

Every public authority possessing information relating to infrastructure projects undertaken by government agencies shall, subject to the provisions of this Act, proactively disclose particulars of each project including its sanctioned cost, timeline for completion, and anticipated beneficiaries. Such disclosure shall be made in a searchable electronic format on the designated website of the respective agency, updated at intervals not exceeding three months. Provided that information pertaining to ongoing tenders or bids may be withheld until the process is finalized and results are publicly announced. The duty of disclosure extends to any amendments affecting project scope or budget, which must also be promptly disseminated. Failure to comply with these requirements shall render the concerned officer liable for penalties as provided herein.

For the purposes of this legislation, an inspection report means a written document prepared by an authorized officer following an inspection conducted pursuant to powers vested under this Act or other applicable laws. Such report shall detail observations pertaining to compliance with relevant regulations and standards, including but not limited to safety protocols, operational procedures, and environmental safeguards. An inspection report may include photographs, diagrams, or supporting data deemed necessary for clarity and accuracy. The authorized officer preparing an inspection report shall ensure its objectivity and impartiality, reflecting only factual findings derived from the physical examination of premises and review of relevant records.

Where any employee or employer considers that any determination made by an adjudicating officer under this Act is erroneous in fact or law, they may within sixty days from the date of receipt of such determination, file an appeal to the Labour Court having jurisdiction over the matter. The appeal shall state specifically the errors alleged to have been committed by the adjudicating officer and grounds upon which it is based. Provided that if the appellant failed to receive notice of the original order, the time limit for filing the appeal shall run from the date on which such notice was actually received or reasonably could have been received. The Labour Court may dismiss the appeal, uphold the determination, or substitute a new determination in place thereof; and any such substituted determination shall be final.

Where any adjudicating officer is satisfied, following due inquiry and affording the concerned party an opportunity for explanation, that a motor vehicle has been used in deviation from the conditions specified under this Act or any rules made thereunder, he may issue a notice directing the owner of such vehicle to appear before him at a time and place mentioned in the notice. Should the owner fail to appear as directed, or if, upon appearance, the adjudicating officer finds evidence substantiating the alleged deviation, he shall impose penalties as prescribed herein. Any party aggrieved by an order passed by the adjudicating officer may appeal within thirty days to the Regional Transport Appellate Authority, subject to payment of such fees as are determined; and the appellate authority’s decision shall be final.

Every consumer complaint received by a District Commission shall be assigned to a competent officer within seven working days of receipt for preliminary assessment. The competent officer shall verify that the complaint discloses a cause of action under this Act and ascertain the territorial jurisdiction of the Commission. Provided that if, upon such assessment, the competent officer finds the complaint frivolous or vexatious, or lacking in merit, he may reject it with reasons recorded in writing. Any party aggrieved by an order rejecting a complaint made under this provision may appeal to the State Commission within thirty days. The State Commission shall review the rejection and pass appropriate orders. A record of all complaints assessed and rejected by a competent officer shall be maintained for audit purposes. Further, any consumer found to repeatedly file frivolous complaints may be subject to penalties as provided herein.

Information furnished under this Act shall be deemed complete only when accompanied by all prescribed particulars relating to the document or data set disclosed, including but not limited to the date of creation, authorial attribution where ascertainable, and any access restrictions previously applied. Failure to provide such prescribed particulars shall constitute a deficiency in the response and render it liable for challenge under Section 18. An appellate authority may, upon review of an appeal alleging deficient disclosure due to omission of prescribed particulars, direct the Public Information Officer to rectify the information or furnish supplementary documentation within a period not exceeding thirty days. Any party dissatisfied with the decision of the appellate authority regarding the adequacy of prescribed particulars may further appeal to the Central Information Commission.

Every public authority obligated under this Act to provide information shall ensure that all documents relating to applications received from citizens are maintained in a manner facilitating ready accessibility. Such maintenance shall include the recording of each application’s date of receipt, the name of the applicant, and a clear description of the requested information. The prescribed particulars regarding the designated Central Information Officer or State Public Information Officer handling an application must be prominently displayed alongside the relevant record. Failure to accurately document these particulars constitutes a violation under this Act. Provided that, where an application is received anonymously, no details need be recorded beyond the date and nature of the request. Subject to exceptions as provided herein, all records pertaining to compliance with these requirements are deemed public information.

Where a claim for compensation arises under this Act relating to injury to or loss of property of a third party caused by a motor vehicle, the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal established under this Act shall adopt a summary procedure for determining the quantum of such compensation. The Tribunal may proceed ex parte if the respondent fails to appear after due notice as provided herein. Provided that, where the claimant is unable to appear personally due to disability or other compelling reasons, the Tribunal may permit representation by an authorized representative. Claims exceeding five hundred thousand rupees shall be subject to further scrutiny and may require additional documentary evidence. The Tribunal shall record its findings concisely and provide reasons for the award. This summary procedure applies irrespective of whether the claim is contested or uncontested under this Act.

Any party obligated to render service under a contract shall perform such obligation in the manner prescribed by the contract itself; provided that if no specific manner is stipulated, performance shall be deemed satisfactory where it conforms to industry standards prevailing at the time of execution. Failure to adhere to the specified or customary manner constitutes a material breach entitling the aggrieved party to damages and injunctive relief. Where the deviation from the agreed manner causes demonstrable prejudice, compensation shall include consequential losses reasonably foreseeable. Repeated instances of non-compliance with the prescribed manner shall be deemed willful default, attracting enhanced penalties as determined by the adjudicating authority. The authority may also order specific performance compelling adherence to the stipulated manner of service.

A generating company seeking to establish a new distribution network for electricity supply shall apply for a certificate of registration from the appropriate State Electricity Regulatory Commission. Such application must detail the proposed geographical area of operation, projected load demand, and planned infrastructure investments. The Commission may grant or reject such application after due consideration of the applicant's technical competence and financial stability, as provided herein. A certificate of registration granted under this Act is assignable subject to prior approval from the Commission; any assignment shall be documented in a prescribed form and filed with the Commission for record. Further, the licensee may license its distribution network or portions thereof to other entities engaged in electricity supply activities, again requiring Commission authorization. The terms and conditions attached to each certificate of registration are binding on all subsequent assignees and licensees.

Where a sole arbitrator appointed pursuant to an arbitration agreement or order of court is unable or unwilling to continue with the proceedings, the High Court may, subject to this Act, appoint a replacement arbitrator. The appointment shall be made after considering applications from suitable candidates and affording the parties concerned an opportunity to present their preferences. An arbitrator so appointed shall possess the same powers and duties as if originally named in the arbitration agreement or order. No act or decision of the original arbitrator shall be deemed invalid solely by reason of his subsequent inability or unwillingness to proceed, provided that any delegation of powers undertaken by him prior to such occurrence remains valid and enforceable under this Act. The parties are entitled to seek redressal for any prejudice arising from an improper exercise of power in appointing a replacement arbitrator.

Registration of Compromise Agreements Affecting Offences Under Contract Law Where parties involved in a dispute concerning contractual obligations agree to settle their differences through compromise, involving an admission or acknowledgement by one party of having committed an offence under this Act, such agreement shall be recorded with the Sub-Registrar of Assurances within thirty days of its execution. The Registrar may require further affidavits from the signatories confirming the voluntary nature and full understanding of the terms contained therein. Any failure to register a compromise agreement as provided herein renders it inadmissible as evidence in subsequent proceedings relating to the underlying offence, subject to an appeal to the District Court on grounds of demonstrable prejudice. Compounding of offences arising from such agreements shall be governed by the principles outlined elsewhere under this Act, and any fees payable for registration shall be prescribed by notification issued by the Central Government.

The Gratuity Records Digitization and Assignment Rules provide that every establishment required to grant gratuity under this Act shall maintain detailed records pertaining to employees’ service history, salary particulars, and computation of terminal benefits. These records shall be maintained electronically or in a durable physical format as determined by the designated authority. The digitization of existing paper-based records is permitted, subject to ensuring data integrity and accessibility as per guidelines issued by the Central Government. Any assignment or transfer of these gratuity records, whether arising from mergers, acquisitions, or restructuring exercises, shall require prior approval from the Gratuity Commissioner. Such assignments must include a formal undertaking guaranteeing continued compliance with obligations under this Act concerning maintenance of records and timely disbursement of gratuity payments.

Any State Government shall, by notification published in the Official Gazette, appoint a competent officer for the purpose of carrying out inspections relating to electricity distribution networks within its jurisdiction. The appointed competent officer shall possess qualifications deemed appropriate by the State Electricity Regulatory Commission, including experience in electrical engineering or related disciplines. Such officers are empowered to enter upon any premises, with due notice as provided herein, where electricity is generated, transmitted, distributed, or consumed, for the purpose of ascertaining compliance with regulations under this Act. The competent officer shall be accompanied by such assistants and technical personnel as may be necessary for conducting thorough inspections. Any person obstructing a competent officer in the exercise of their powers shall be deemed to have violated provisions relating to obstruction of public servants. Records pertaining to inspections conducted by a competent officer shall be maintained securely and made available to relevant authorities upon request.

Where a public authority leases premises for its administrative functions, the terms of the lease agreement shall stipulate that a security deposit, not exceeding three months’ rent, is to be furnished by the lessee. Such security deposit shall be held in an interest-bearing account maintained by the lessor and may only be utilized to cover damages to the leased property beyond normal wear and tear or for outstanding dues owed by the lessee under the terms of the lease. Any portion of the security deposit remaining after satisfaction of such obligations, as determined through a joint assessment conducted within thirty days of the termination of the lease, shall be promptly returned to the lessee. The public authority is obligated to ensure compliance with these provisions when entering into any new lease agreement or renewing existing ones, subject to prevailing regulations under this Act.

For the purposes of this Act, an adjudicating officer means a person appointed by the Central Government or State Government, as applicable, to exercise the powers and discharge the duties conferred upon him or her under this Act relating to the adjudication of disputes concerning violations of consumer rights. An adjudicating officer shall possess experience in law or administration, with specific consideration given to familiarity with principles of natural justice and administrative procedures. The Central Government may prescribe qualifications for an adjudicating officer by notification in the Official Gazette. Subject to any rules made under this Act, the functions of an adjudicating officer include receiving complaints, conducting inquiries, and passing orders as provided herein.

Where a motor vehicle is suspected to have been used in connection with an offence punishable under this Act, or where there are reasonable grounds to believe that evidence relating to such an offence may be found within the vehicle, any police officer not below the rank of Inspector shall possess the power of entry. This power extends to entering and searching any premises wherein a motor vehicle is kept, subject to obtaining prior authorization from a Magistrate First Class or higher authority, except in cases where there exists imminent danger that evidence will be destroyed or tampered with. The person exercising this power of entry shall provide written notice, if reasonably possible, detailing the purpose of the search and the officer’s identity. Any goods seized during such an exercise are subject to proper inventory documentation as provided herein. Compensation for any damage caused during the exercise of this power may be claimed by the affected party under provisions relating to tortious liability.

The Central Information Commission may, through notification published in the Official Gazette, authorize any public authority to designate specific officers as Inspectors for the purpose of facilitating access to records under this Act. Such designation shall not preclude a public authority from appointing additional Inspectors at its discretion. An Inspector so authorized shall be deemed to hold office during the pleasure of the Central Information Commission and may, subject to regulations prescribed by the Commission, grant licenses permitting third parties to conduct inspections of designated records. Any license granted is transferable, provided that such transfer is approved by the Commission and accompanied by a fee as determined under this Act. The original licensee shall remain liable for any breaches occurring prior to the assignment. A comprehensive inspection report documenting findings during licensed access must be submitted to both the public authority and the Central Information Commission.

For the purposes of this Act, an appellate tribunal is constituted for adjudicating appeals arising from orders passed by Public Information Officers or Appellate Authorities under this Act. The appellate tribunal shall consist of a Chairperson appointed by the Central Government and not less than two other members also appointed by the Central Government. Members shall possess experience in law, public administration, management, or information technology. The functions of the appellate tribunal include hearing appeals, considering relevant documents presented before it, and issuing orders as provided herein. Decisions of the appellate tribunal shall be binding on the parties involved subject to appeal under any other law for the time being in force.

Any person found to have manufactured, sold, distributed, imported, or exported food in violation of standards prescribed under this Act shall be liable to pay a monetary penalty not exceeding two lakh rupees for the first offence; subsequent offences may attract penalties up to five lakh rupees. The adjudicating officer, upon receiving a complaint or information regarding such violations, shall issue a notice requiring the alleged offender to appear and present their case within thirty days. Failure to comply with the notice or demonstrating persistent non-compliance will result in an ex parte order issued by the adjudicating officer determining the appropriate penalty. Appeals against orders passed by the adjudicating officer may be made to the appellate authority as provided herein, subject to a fee of ten thousand rupees.

Where any officer authorised under this Act reasonably suspects that any food is unsafe or improperly stored, or that any violation of regulations prescribed herein has occurred, such officer may exercise the power of entry into any premises for the purpose of conducting an inspection and taking samples; provided that before exercising such power of entry, the officer shall, if possible, give notice to the occupier of the premises, stating the reasons for such intended entry. Failure to provide such notice shall not, however, invalidate subsequent findings under this Act. Any person obstructing an authorised officer in the exercise of their power of entry shall be deemed guilty of an offence and liable to penalty as provided herein. Disputes regarding the reasonableness of a suspected violation may be raised before the adjudicating officer within thirty days of the inspection.

Revocation of gratuity, once determined and paid in accordance with the provisions herein, shall not thereafter be permitted except where fraud or misrepresentation has been established. For the purposes of this Act, "fraud" includes any wilful suppression of material facts relating to an employee’s length of service or salary; “misrepresentation” means a false statement made by the employer which induces the employee to believe he is entitled to gratuity. The determination of whether fraud or misrepresentation has occurred shall be subject to judicial review, and the burden of proving such grounds of revocation lies entirely upon the petitioner seeking reversal of the gratuity payment.

Any enterprise establishing or operating an industrial unit within a designated ecologically sensitive zone shall provide, prior to commencement of operations, a security deposit to the competent authority, the amount thereof determined based upon the potential environmental impact assessment report submitted under this Act. Such security deposit shall be held in trust and may be forfeited wholly or partially if any violation of prescribed environmental standards occurs, including but not limited to discharge of effluents beyond permissible limits or non-compliance with waste management protocols. The competent authority may require replenishment of the security deposit following remediation measures undertaken by the enterprise. Reimbursement of the security deposit, less any amounts utilized for remedial actions as provided herein, shall be permitted upon satisfactory completion of the operational period and demonstration of continued compliance.

The licensing of certified document examiners operating within jurisdictions recognized under this Act shall be subject to a schedule of fees as determined by the Central Board for Forensic Sciences and Criminal Investigation. Any individual or entity seeking authorization to provide forensic document examination services must submit an application accompanied by the requisite fee, which is detailed in the aforementioned schedule. Assignment of rights pertaining to examination reports generated by certified examiners may occur only with prior written consent from both the examiner and the original client, provided that such assignment does not compromise the integrity or confidentiality of the evidence. The Board may, subject to due process, levy additional charges for expedited processing of applications or re-examination requests. Further, any transfer of a license shall incur a fee as prescribed within the schedule; this includes instances where ownership of an examination practice changes hands.

Where a contract involves the inspection of goods or immovable property prior to its execution, the right to inspect shall accrue to the party seeking such inspection as an inherent condition precedent to finalization. Failure by the seller or vendor to permit reasonable and timely inspection, or providing access to a misrepresented state of the subject matter, shall constitute a material breach entitling the prospective buyer or lessee to rescind the contract without liability. Any subsequent claim for damages arising from this breach may be pursued under general principles of contractual remedy. The aggrieved party shall have the burden of proving that reasonable opportunity for inspection was denied and that such denial materially impacted their decision-making process. An *inspection report* prepared by a qualified professional, if presented, shall be admissible as evidence regarding the condition of the goods or property at the time of intended purchase, subject to cross-examination.

Where a contract is induced by misrepresentation concerning the quality or nature of goods offered for sale, and the buyer discovers such misrepresentation within six months of the date of purchase, the buyer shall be entitled to claim rescission of the contract from the seller. Such right of rescission may be exercised only if the buyer has not materially altered the condition of the goods following discovery of the misrepresentation. The seller shall be liable to refund any amount paid by the buyer under the contract upon its rescission. Any dispute concerning whether a representation constitutes material inducement or whether the buyer’s actions have precluded their right to rescind shall be determined by a competent officer appointed for this purpose, whose decision shall be final and binding. This remedy is without prejudice to any claim for damages which the buyer may otherwise pursue under this Act.

Where compensation is claimed for injury sustained in respect of loss of baggage or personal effects accompanying a motor vehicle during carriage, the insurer shall be liable to pay such compensation only if the claimant establishes that the damage or loss arose directly from an act or omission attributable to the driver or operator of the vehicle, and not due to inherent vice or pre-existing condition of the property. The manner of service relating to notification of claims under this provision is governed by Form A annexed hereto; failure to adhere strictly to the requirements of that form shall render the claim inadmissible. Provided that, any party disputing the admissibility of a claim based on non-compliance with Form A may appeal to the Motor Accidents Settlement Tribunal within thirty days of the order rejecting the claim.

Registration of documents relating to immovable property shall be deemed conclusive evidence of the fact of execution thereof, subject to any inquiry under this Act regarding forgery or fraud. Where a document affecting an interest in property is presented for registration, the Registrar shall require satisfactory proof of identity and authority of all parties concerned, including verification by oath or affirmation where prescribed. Any person claiming adversely to such registered deed may institute legal proceedings; however, such claim shall be barred if the claimant fails to commence action within thirty years from the date of registration. The period of limitation as provided herein is applicable irrespective of any subsequent transfer or encumbrance on the property. This provision applies equally to documents executed before and after the commencement of this legislation.

For the purposes of this Act, a certificate of registration is a document issued by the Regional Transport Authority or an authority authorized thereunder, evidencing ownership of a motor vehicle and granting permission for its operation on public roads. The certificate shall contain particulars relating to the make, model, chassis number, engine number, registered owner, address, class of vehicle, fuel type, and seating capacity as determined under this Act. A certificate of registration may be transferred upon sale or otherwise disposal of a motor vehicle, subject to conditions prescribed herein. Any alteration to details recorded on the certificate requires notification to and approval by the registering authority.
