Where gratuity is payable to the legal heirs of a deceased employee, or where the whereabouts of an employee are unascertainable, the employer shall pursue all available means for determining the identity of the claimant and verifying their entitlement under this Act. Upon failure to identify a legitimate claimant within six months from the date gratuity becomes due, the amount may be deposited with the Controlling Authority. The Controlling Authority shall issue notice to the public, specifying the amount and details pertaining to the deceased employee, inviting claims subject to verification as provided herein. Any claim received after the expiry of three years from the date of such publication shall be deemed invalid unless proof satisfactory to the Controlling Authority is furnished demonstrating due diligence in attempting identification prior to that period. The employer remains responsible for any subsequent recovery of dues arising from an erroneous payment made during this process.

Where documents are produced for inspection pursuant to a summons or requisition issued under this Act, the officer authorized to take depositions may require any person present to state whether they possess knowledge relevant to the contents of those documents. Such questioning shall be conducted in the presence of counsel representing the party issuing the summons and the individual whose testimony is sought. The presiding authority shall determine whether an individual qualifies as a competent officer for this purpose, considering their rank, training, and experience within the relevant government department. Any challenge to the designation of a competent officer may be raised before the authority and its determination shall be final, subject to appeal to the High Court on grounds limited to jurisdictional error or demonstrable bias.

Where a contract stipulates the provision of a security deposit by one party to another, such deposit shall be held in trust by the recipient until all obligations under the agreement have been fully discharged. The amount of the security deposit shall correspond precisely with the sum agreed upon within the contractual terms; any deviation from this stipulated sum renders the deposit invalid. Upon satisfactory completion of the contracted work or delivery of goods as per the agreement, the security deposit shall be promptly returned to the original provider, free of interest unless explicitly stated otherwise under this Act. Provided that, in instances of breach of contract or failure to meet agreed-upon performance standards, the recipient may retain all or a portion of the security deposit as liquidated damages, subject to judicial review and assessment.

Registration of commercial vehicles shall proceed through a summary procedure designed for expeditious allocation of vehicle registrations within designated zones. Every individual or entity seeking registration of a motor vehicle for commercial purposes must submit Form MV-C1 along with proof of ownership, valid insurance documentation, and evidence of payment of applicable fees. The registering authority may request additional documents as deemed necessary to verify the applicant’s eligibility under this Act. Provided that applicants demonstrating compliance with all stipulated requirements shall have their registration processed within seven working days. Failure to provide requisite information or demonstrable non-compliance will result in rejection of the application, and a revised application may be submitted after rectifying deficiencies. The authority is empowered to conduct inspections as necessary to ensure vehicle suitability for commercial operation.

Every application for a licence under this Act shall be accompanied by a detailed layout plan indicating the premises intended to be used for food handling activities, including storage areas, processing equipment, and waste disposal systems. The Licensing Authority shall verify that the proposed layout complies with the hygiene requirements as provided herein and ensures adequate segregation of raw materials from finished products. No licence shall be granted until the applicant furnishes proof of registration with a recognized institution providing training in food safety practices for all personnel involved in handling food. The conditions of licence may include, but are not limited to, restrictions on the types of food manufactured or processed, limits on production capacity, and mandatory adherence to prescribed standards for packaging materials. Any alteration to the layout plan after grant of a licence shall require prior approval from the Licensing Authority, who may inspect the premises at any reasonable time to ensure compliance with these regulations. Failure to comply with the conditions of licence is subject to penalties as determined under this Act.

The registration of a motor vehicle shall remain valid subject to its continued compliance with conditions specified herein; however, such registration is liable for revocation in circumstances defined below. Grounds of revocation include, but are not limited to, the discovery of material misstatement or suppression of fact during the application process, persistent and willful violation of traffic regulations as determined by a competent authority, fraudulent activities related to insurance claims involving the vehicle, and alterations made to the vehicle’s chassis or engine without prior authorization. Further, registration may be revoked if the registered owner fails to maintain adequate third-party liability insurance coverage as provided herein.

Where performance of contractual obligations is rendered impossible due to unforeseen circumstances, the question of whether such impossibility excuses non-performance shall be determined with reference to the specific terms agreed upon by the contracting parties and the prevailing commercial practices at the time of contract formation. It shall be further considered that any stipulation regarding the manner of service, including but not limited to delivery schedules or communication protocols, is deemed a material term unless explicitly waived or modified in writing. Disputes arising from alleged deviations from the stipulated manner of service may be subject to arbitration as provided herein, and the arbitrator’s decision shall be final, barring appeals based solely on demonstrable procedural irregularities during the arbitral proceedings.

For the purposes of this Act, “material information” relating to food products means particulars concerning the composition, ingredients, additives, processing methods, origin, or potential allergens present in any food article that would reasonably influence the purchasing decision of a consumer. A manufacturer or importer shall have a duty of disclosure regarding material information pertaining to their food products. This duty extends to ensuring such information is prominently displayed on packaging and accompanying documentation. Failure to adequately disclose material information constitutes a violation under this Act, subject to penalties as provided herein. The Central Food Safety Authority may issue guidelines specifying the manner in which this duty of disclosure shall be fulfilled.

Registration of agreements for compounding of offences relating to violations under this Act shall be undertaken exclusively through the designated online portal maintained by the Central Information Commission. Every agreement proposing the compounding of an offence, including but not limited to instances of wilful obstruction or failure to furnish information as provided herein, must be submitted electronically in the prescribed format. The agreement shall detail the nature of the violation, the proposed sum for compounding, and a declaration from both the offender and the Public Information Officer involved. Such agreements are subject to review by a Committee constituted under sub-section (3) of section 58. No compounding shall take effect until its registration is confirmed on the portal, signifying approval by the aforementioned Committee.

The Public Authority shall maintain all records diligently and in a manner facilitating access as provided herein, including but not limited to electronic formats where feasible. Any officer authorized under this Act may grant licenses for the reproduction of any record held by the Public Authority, subject to such terms and conditions relating to quality control and data integrity as determined by the Central Information Commission. Such licenses shall be assignable in whole or in part with the prior written consent of the Public Authority, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld. The fees payable for assignment under this provision shall be remitted to the designated government account. No license granted hereunder shall permit alteration or modification of any record without express authorization from the Central Information Commission; and the maintenance of records remains paramount.

The Central Information Commission shall, upon receiving a request from a Public Authority seeking authorisation for delegation of powers relating to the processing of information requests, examine whether the proposed delegation complies with the principles of transparency and accountability enshrined under this Act. Such delegation shall only be permitted where the authority demonstrates that it possesses adequate mechanisms for oversight and redressal concerning actions undertaken by the delegated officer. The request must detail the specific functions being delegated, the qualifications and training provided to the designated officer, and procedures ensuring compliance with time limits prescribed herein. Provided that no power relating to the imposition of penalties or adjudication of complaints may be delegated under this Act. Any delegation shall be reviewed annually by the Public Authority and reported to the Commission.

Registration of Consumer Grievance Redressal Forums shall be undertaken through a centralized digital portal maintained by the Central Consumer Protection Authority, requiring submission of Form-A detailing the composition and jurisdiction of each Forum. Every registered Forum shall maintain an updated register of cases filed, disposed of, and pending, accessible for public inspection during stipulated hours. Where an offence under this Act is committed, and parties are amenable, the Forum may facilitate compounding of offences subject to conditions prescribed by regulations framed by the Central Government. Such compounding settlements must be recorded in Form-B and uploaded onto the digital portal within seven days of agreement, ensuring transparency and accountability as provided herein. Failure to register a settlement or maintain accurate records shall render the Forum liable for penalties determined under this Act.

Every manufacturer, packer, importer, distributor, retailer or vendor of food products shall diligently maintain a register of undertakings involved in the handling of their respective food articles, accessible for inspection by authorized officers under this Act. This register shall include the name and address of each undertaking, details regarding the nature of its involvement – whether as processor, transporter, storage facility operator, or otherwise – and confirmation that such undertaking possesses all requisite licenses and registrations as provided herein. The Food Safety Officer may require submission of a certified copy of this register upon request. Any alteration to an entry in the register shall be clearly indicated with date and reason for change, duly authenticated by a responsible person. Failure to maintain such a register or providing false information therein will render the offender liable to penalties as prescribed under this Act.

Where a person possesses or controls any document which he is required by law to produce, or which contains information material to any question in issue before a court, he shall be deemed to have a duty of disclosure relating to the contents thereof. This duty extends to providing copies or extracts from such documents as the Court may direct, provided that the production is made within the time specified by the Court and under conditions safeguarding confidentiality where applicable. Failure to comply with this duty without reasonable excuse, which shall be determined at the discretion of the presiding officer, renders the person liable for costs incurred by any party demonstrating prejudice arising from such non-disclosure. The Court may, in its judgment, further impose a penalty not exceeding fifty thousand rupees as compensation for wilful disregard of this provision. Any officer receiving information pursuant to this duty shall maintain strict neutrality and report findings accurately under this Act.

Every license issued under this Act for the manufacture, processing, handling, packaging, storage, distribution or sale of food products shall be accompanied by a security deposit, the amount of which shall be determined by the Licensing Officer based on the scale of operation and potential risk assessment as provided herein. Such security deposit shall be payable to the Food Safety and Standards Authority and may be forfeited in cases of violation of regulations pertaining to hygiene, adulteration, or misbranding of food products. The licensee shall be entitled to a refund of the security deposit upon expiry or revocation of the license, subject to due audit and verification of compliance with all applicable provisions under this Act. Assignment of a license requires prior written consent from the Authority and transfer of the associated security deposit in accordance with prescribed procedures; failure to comply will render the assignment void.

For the purposes of this Act, “material fact” with respect to insurance coverage means information concerning the vehicle’s history, including but not limited to prior accidents, claims filed, and modifications undertaken that could reasonably affect the assessment of risk by an insurer. A person offering or selling motor vehicle insurance shall have a duty of disclosure regarding any material facts known to them. This duty extends to disclosing such facts to the prospective policyholder in clear and understandable language. Failure to disclose a material fact constitutes a breach of this Act, subject to penalties as provided herein. The determination of whether information is “material” shall be based on industry standards and prevailing legal precedent.

Any consumer or licensee aggrieved by an order passed by a State Electricity Regulatory Commission relating to tariff determination, license conditions, or enforcement actions may file an appeal before the appropriate appellate tribunal. The appeal shall be made within sixty days from the date of communication of the order and must specify the grounds upon which it is based, including any material facts not previously brought to the attention of the regulatory commission. Subject to just cause shown, no appeal shall be admitted after the expiry of that period. The appellate tribunal may, after affording an opportunity for hearing to all parties concerned, confirm, vary, or reverse the order appealed against and may substitute its own order in lieu thereof. Any party aggrieved by an order of the appellate tribunal may further seek redressal under this Act.

All documents pertaining to land registration executed within a Sub-Registrar’s jurisdiction shall be preserved permanently under this Act. The Registrar appointed for each district shall maintain a central repository for all recorded instruments, ensuring accessibility for authorized personnel and designated government agencies. Particular care shall be taken during the digitization process of these records; any alteration or omission discovered after digital capture necessitates immediate rectification and annotation within the system log. Records relating to immovable property transferred through gift or will shall be subject to enhanced scrutiny as provided herein. The Sub-Registrar is obligated to ensure proper indexing and cross-referencing for efficient retrieval, facilitating public access consistent with privacy regulations. Maintenance of records constitutes a fundamental duty under this Act, and any negligence in preservation may attract penalties as determined by the competent authority.

Any party to a contract involving goods subject to an inspection report shall be deemed to have fulfilled their obligations regarding quality and condition only upon submission of said report to the other contracting party within fourteen days of delivery. Failure to submit the inspection report as provided herein constitutes a material breach, rendering the defaulting party liable for damages including but not limited to loss of profits and consequential losses suffered by the aggrieved party. The inspecting officer whose report is submitted shall be subject to penalties under this Act if it is proven that the report was falsified or deliberately misleading. Any challenge to the validity of an inspection report must be brought before a designated arbitration panel within thirty days of its issuance; otherwise, the findings contained therein shall be final and binding.

An employee aggrieved by the withholding or delayed payment of gratuity may file a complaint with the Controlling Authority constituted under this Act within six months from the date gratuity became due, detailing the circumstances leading to such non-payment and specifying the amount claimed. The Authority shall entertain complaints even if the employee has previously accepted any sum in settlement, provided that it is demonstrated that such acceptance was obtained through coercion or misrepresentation by the employer. Grounds of revocation of an order passed by the Controlling Authority are limited solely to demonstrable errors of fact or law apparent on the face of the record and may only be sought through a revision petition before the appellate authority as provided herein. The employee shall be entitled to interest at such rate as the Central Government may specify, calculated from the date gratuity was originally due until actual payment.

The gratuity payable under this Act relating to services rendered prior to a change of ownership or control of an establishment may be assigned by the employer to any third party, including but not limited to financial institutions providing loans or advances against future gratuity payments. Such assignment shall include all rights, title and interest in respect of the gratuity liability, subject to the conditions stipulated within the agreement of assignment. The assignor shall remain liable for ensuring compliance with the provisions relating to eligibility and computation under this Act. Any action brought by an employee to recover gratuity after the expiry of the period of limitation prescribed herein, or arising from a claim related to an assigned gratuity liability, shall be deemed barred unless leave to sue is obtained from the Labour Court.

Where a gratuity liability arises from the assignment of an establishment or a portion thereof, or from the amalgamation of establishments, the employer succeeding to the business shall be deemed to be the ‘employer’ for the purposes of this Act and shall assume all existing gratuity obligations pertaining to employees previously employed by the transferring entity. The duty of disclosure regarding such assumed liabilities shall extend to providing detailed schedules of accrued but unpaid gratuities to the successor employer within thirty days of the assignment or amalgamation taking effect. Failure to provide a complete and accurate schedule constitutes an actionable default under this Act, subject to penalties as prescribed. Any third party acquiring rights related to the transferred establishment may request access to such disclosure documentation from the successor employer, provided that reasonable confidentiality concerns are addressed as determined by the Gratuity Controller.

Any agreement recorded in a terms of settlement executed pursuant to a decree or order of a civil court shall be enforceable as if it were a contract under this Act. Provided that, any party seeking enforcement of such terms may only do so within three years from the date of execution; failure to initiate proceedings within said period shall constitute a bar to recovery. Where a breach occurs in respect of obligations contained within the terms of settlement, the aggrieved party shall be entitled to claim damages as determined by the court. The court may, upon finding evidence of fraudulent misrepresentation or coercion during the negotiation and execution of such terms, refuse enforcement notwithstanding adherence to the prescribed timelines. Any penalty for non-compliance with the terms shall be recoverable as a civil debt.

Where any information requested under this Act is held within a premises which is secured or locked, the Central Information Commission may, subject to providing twenty-four hours’ written notice to the designated Public Information Officer and the occupier of the premises, authorize an officer empowered by the Commission to exercise a power of entry into such premises for the purpose of inspecting records relevant to the information sought. Provided that if reasonable cause exists to believe that delay in obtaining access would frustrate the purpose of the request, the Central Information Commission may waive the requirement of prior notice. Any person obstructing or attempting to obstruct an officer exercising a power of entry as provided herein shall be deemed guilty of an offence and liable for prosecution under applicable laws. An appeal against such authorization lies before the appellate authority.

Where any dispute arises concerning the appointment or conduct of an appointed authority under this Act, either party may file an objection with the designated judicial forum within thirty days from the date of the action complained of. Such objection shall be accompanied by a statement detailing the grounds for challenge and supported by all relevant documentation. The judicial forum shall provide both parties with a notice period of fifteen days prior to any hearing. An order passed by the appointed authority may be appealed to the appellate authority, provided that the appeal is filed within sixty days of the original decision. Any interlocutory orders issued during the proceedings before the appellate authority are subject to review under procedures as provided herein.

For the purposes of this Act, “summary procedure” means an expedited process for adjudicating violations involving minor infractions relating to food safety standards, where the penalty proposed does not exceed two thousand rupees. Such procedure shall involve a single designated officer authorized under this Act, who may issue a notice specifying the alleged violation and providing an opportunity for the accused to submit a written response within seven days. The officer shall then render a decision based solely on the written submissions, without oral arguments or formal hearings. This summary procedure is available only where the Food Safety Officer deems it appropriate, subject to guidelines prescribed by the Central Government.

Where a register of undertakings is maintained by an entity registered under the Companies Act, 2013, or any other legislation governing corporate bodies, access to such register shall be deemed public information subject to reasonable restrictions as may be prescribed by regulations framed thereunder. Any person claiming that their rights have been prejudiced due to unauthorized disclosure or manipulation of entries within a register of undertakings may apply to the appropriate jurisdictional authority for redressal. The authority shall entertain such applications and issue directions, including but not limited to orders for compensation, rectification of records, and punitive action against responsible parties. Provided that any information pertaining to personal data contained within the register shall be protected under the provisions relating to data privacy as provided herein. Under this Act, failure to maintain an accurate and accessible register of undertakings constitutes a civil offence, punishable with a fine not exceeding one lakh rupees.

A statutory declaration is a written statement voluntarily made by an individual before an authorized officer, affirming its truthfulness to the best of their knowledge and belief. For the purposes of admissibility under this Act, a statutory declaration shall be in the form specified in Schedule A and shall contain a clear and unequivocal assertion regarding the facts stated therein. The declarant shall sign the document in the presence of the authorized officer, who shall administer an oath or affirmation confirming the veracity of the contents. Any person making a false statement within a statutory declaration is liable for penalties as provided herein.

The license granted to a distribution licensee for the supply of electricity within its licensed area may be assigned, subject to prior approval from the State Commission, provided that the proposed assignee possesses adequate technical expertise and financial resources as determined by the Commission. Such assignment shall not include any rights or obligations pertaining to generation licenses held by the assignor unless specifically consented to in writing by the generator. Any sub-license granted under this Act is also subject to similar approval requirements. The adjudicating officer may, upon receiving a complaint regarding unauthorized assignment or attempted transfer of a distribution license, issue notices and conduct hearings as deemed necessary. Failure to obtain prior consent for an assignment shall render the assignee liable to penalties as prescribed herein and may result in revocation of the sub-license.

Where a dispute arises between a food vendor and a consumer regarding the quality or safety of food supplied, either party may initiate proceedings seeking resolution through mediation facilitated by a designated officer appointed under this Act. Such mediation shall proceed in accordance with prescribed procedures detailed in Schedule B. The designated officer shall maintain a record of all attempts at amicable settlement and any offers made during such process. Should an agreement be reached between the parties, it shall be documented as terms of settlement, signed by both vendor and consumer, and authenticated by the designated officer. These terms of settlement will have the force of a decree passed by a civil court, subject to appeal under the relevant provisions of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908. Failure to adhere to the terms of settlement may result in penalties as provided herein.

Where a food business operator fails to comply with prescribed standards of quality or safety, or engages in unfair trade practices relating to food, a complaint may be filed before the adjudicating officer appointed under this Act. The adjudicating officer shall afford the complainant and the accused food business operator an opportunity for hearing, including cross-examination of witnesses, subject to principles of natural justice. Upon finding a violation, the adjudicating officer may impose penalties as provided herein, which include monetary fines not exceeding [amount] or suspension of license. Any party aggrieved by an order passed by the adjudicating officer may appeal to the appellate authority within sixty days from the date of such order. The appellate authority shall consider all relevant evidence and may affirm, modify, or reverse the original decision.

Where a consumer alleges unfair trade practice or deficiency in service by a seller or service provider, an authorized officer appointed under this Act may exercise the power of entry upon such premises as are reasonably believed to contain evidence relevant to the investigation. Such entry shall be subject to providing written notice to the person appearing to be in charge, unless circumstances render immediate action necessary to prevent destruction of evidence or continued violation. The consumer aggrieved shall have the right to request a copy of any record obtained during such entry and to challenge its admissibility in subsequent proceedings before appropriate forums. Provided that an officer exercising this power shall produce identification confirming their authority and act with due respect for the rights of persons affected, ensuring minimal disruption to business operations as far as practicable.

Where a dispute arises concerning the quality or safety of any food product subject to regulation under this Act, and the concerned parties are unable to resolve the matter through informal mediation, they may elect to enter into terms of settlement which shall be in writing and duly signed by all involved parties or their authorized representatives. Such terms of settlement, if accepted by the adjudicating officer upon review, shall have the force of an order passed under this Act and shall be binding on all parties thereto. Any party aggrieved by a term included within such terms of settlement may file an appeal before the Food Safety Appellate Tribunal within sixty days from the date of its acceptance by the adjudicating officer; provided that the appellate tribunal may dismiss any appeal if it determines the dispute was fairly addressed in the original settlement.

Any person who has reason to believe that an environmental violation is occurring within any premises shall report such belief to the nearest Regional Officer appointed under this Act. Upon receiving such a report, or acting on its own initiative, the Regional Officer may direct an investigation into the alleged violation. For the purpose of conducting such investigations, and subject to ensuring minimal disruption to ongoing operations, the Regional Officer or any officer duly authorised by them shall have power of entry upon any premises reasonably suspected of harbouring conditions violating environmental standards as provided herein. Such entry shall be accompanied by a written notice served on the occupier of the premises, detailing the purpose of the inspection and the names of the officers entering. The occupier is obliged to facilitate such entry and provide access to relevant documents or information. Failure to comply with this direction may render the occupier liable for penalties under this Act.

The Central Licensing Authority shall determine the schedule of fees payable for various licences issued under this Act, including but not limited to those relating to food processing units, storage facilities, and transportation vehicles. Such fees shall be commensurate with the complexity of inspection required and the risk assessment undertaken prior to issuance. Assignment of a licence, whether partial or complete, requires prior written consent from the Authority, subject to submission of an application detailing the proposed assignee's qualifications and financial stability. A fee equivalent to twenty-five percent of the original license fee shall be levied for each assignment approved under this provision. Further, any transfer of ownership in a licensed establishment necessitates notification to the Authority within thirty days, accompanied by updated documentation verifying compliance with all applicable regulations as provided herein. The schedule of fees may be revised periodically based on prevailing administrative costs and inflation indices.

Where an employer fails to provide a written statement of account detailing gratuity entitlements to an employee prior to their termination or retirement, such failure shall constitute a breach of duty of disclosure under this Act. The aggrieved employee may appeal the determination of gratuity amount resulting from said omission before the Grievance Redressal Committee constituted under Section 7, provided that the appeal is filed within ninety days from the date of receipt of the communication detailing the gratuity calculation. Any order passed by the Grievance Redressal Committee shall be final, subject to a further appeal to the Labour Court on grounds of perversity or demonstrable error in law. The employer shall bear the burden of proving compliance with all relevant provisions regarding gratuity calculations and disclosures.

An application for registration of an arbitration agreement or a list of arbitrators shall be submitted to the registering authority in the prescribed form, accompanied by all relevant documents establishing the validity and scope of the agreement or the qualifications of the listed individuals. The applicant shall pay such fees as may be determined by the Central Government from time to time. Upon receipt of the application and verification of its completeness, the registering authority shall issue a certificate of registration within thirty days, provided that any deficiency in the submitted documentation shall necessitate a request for rectification from the applicant, extending the processing timeline accordingly. The register maintained under this Act shall be open to public inspection during specified hours. Any party aggrieved by the refusal or delay in issuance of a certificate of registration may appeal to the appellate authority as provided herein.

Every public authority obligated under this Act to provide information relating to its activities shall ensure that all inspection reports pertaining to infrastructure projects undertaken by it are maintained in a manner readily accessible for public scrutiny. Such inspection reports, including those generated by third-party contractors or consultants engaged for project oversight, shall be deemed ‘information’ as defined herein and subject to the provisions regarding disclosure. The Central Information Commission may, upon receiving a complaint, direct a public authority to rectify any deficiencies in the maintenance of these inspection reports, provided that redaction is permissible only under conditions stipulated by this Act. Further, an applicant requesting access to an inspection report shall be entitled to receive a certified copy thereof unless it contains trade secrets or confidential commercial information, subject to applicable exemptions.

Where gratuity is payable under this Act, the fees for verification of service certificates submitted by employers to the Controlling Authority shall be determined according to a schedule of fees published by the Central Government from time to time. Such schedule shall prescribe different rates based on the number of employees covered by the certificate and the geographical location of the establishment submitting it. An employer seeking expedited processing of a gratuity claim, as defined under this Act, may pay an additional fee not exceeding twenty-five percent of the prescribed rate; provided that such request is accompanied by a duly signed application to the Controlling Authority. The Central Government may, through notification, revise the schedule of fees periodically, subject to consultation with representatives of employers and employees.

Where any food business operator alleges that action taken by a Food Safety Officer under this Act is without due cause or in excess of powers, they may within ninety days from the date of communication of such action appeal to the State Food Safety Appellate Authority. The appellate authority shall consider all relevant materials and hear representations from both the aggrieved party and the concerned food safety officer. Provided that if the appellant fails to make an appeal within the prescribed period of limitation, the order shall be deemed final. Any order passed by the State Food Safety Appellate Authority may be further appealed against under this Act, subject to a further period of limitation of sixty days from the date of communication of the appellate authority’s decision.

Every driver found guilty of an offence relating to overloading beyond the prescribed limits shall be liable to pay a compounding fee not exceeding five thousand rupees. The Transport Department may, subject to due process and after providing opportunity for hearing, direct seizure of the vehicle until payment of the said fee is made. Failure to remit the compounding fee within thirty days from the date of issuance of notice shall render the driver liable to prosecution under this Act. Further, in cases involving habitual overloading, where a driver has been compounded three or more times within a period of one year, the registering authority may suspend the driving licence for a minimum period of six months. The compounding of offences does not preclude further action as deemed necessary by the court.

An application for a certificate of registration under this Act shall be submitted electronically through the Food Safety and Standards Authority’s designated portal, accompanied by a non-refundable processing fee as determined by notification issued by the Central Government. The application shall include detailed information regarding the nature of food business operations, premises layout plans conforming to hygienic standards, and a list of all directors or partners responsible for compliance with regulations. Any alteration to the particulars furnished in the original application requires submission of an amended form within thirty days, subject to applicable fees. Failure to disclose material information may render the certificate liable for cancellation. The Authority may conduct inspections prior to issuing a certificate of registration to verify adherence to prescribed guidelines and standards as provided herein.

Any officer authorized under this Act to receive fees relating to the presentation of evidence, examination of witnesses, or any other process governed by these regulations shall adhere strictly to the schedule of fees prescribed in the First Schedule annexed hereto. Failure to remit collected fees within thirty days of receipt will attract a penalty equivalent to ten percent of the total amount due, payable to the Government treasury. Any employee found to have knowingly understated the fees received for personal gain shall be deemed guilty of an offense and subject to disciplinary action, including dismissal from service, without prejudice to criminal prosecution under relevant penal laws. The prescribed schedule of fees may be revised periodically by notification in the Official Gazette; such revisions shall take effect prospectively.

For the purposes of adjudicating disputes concerning consumer rights under this Act, an “adjudicating officer” means an individual appointed by the State Government, possessing qualifications in law or management, and specifically designated to exercise the powers and discharge the duties conferred upon them herein. An adjudicating officer shall be empowered to conduct hearings, examine evidence presented by parties, and record findings of fact. The appointment of an adjudicating officer may be subject to such terms and conditions as are determined by the State Government. Any individual acting in the capacity of an adjudicating officer is deemed a public servant within the meaning of relevant penal provisions.

Every Public Information Officer receiving a notice of demand for information under this Act shall, within seven working days from the date of receipt, serve upon the applicant an acknowledgement containing the reference number and date of the said notice. Failure to comply with this provision shall render the Public Information Officer liable to a penalty of twenty-five rupees for each day of default, subject to a maximum aggregate of five thousand rupees. The Central Information Commission may, after giving the concerned Public Information Officer an opportunity of being heard, impose such penalties as it deems fit, provided that the imposition of any penalty shall not preclude the applicant from pursuing remedies available under this Act.

Where any vehicle is involved in an accident resulting in injury or death, the registering authority shall maintain records pertaining to the prescribed particulars of that vehicle, including but not limited to its registration certificate, insurance policy, and fitness validation documents. Failure to accurately record these details constitutes a violation under this Act and renders the registering officer liable for disciplinary action. Disputes concerning the accuracy or completeness of such recorded particulars may be raised by any claimant seeking compensation, and shall be adjudicated by the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal. The tribunal’s determination on the veracity of prescribed particulars is final, provided that the claimant demonstrates demonstrable prejudice arising from inaccuracies; appeals against this finding are permitted only on grounds of perversity.

Where a food business operator offers or exposes any packaged commodity for sale, they shall conspicuously display upon such package, in clear and legible language, all information pertaining to ingredients, nutritional value, expiry date, and weight net of packing, as provided herein. Failure to comply with this requirement constitutes a violation under this Act and renders the operator liable for penalty. Any consumer demonstrating demonstrable prejudice resulting from a failure by a food business operator to fulfill their duty of disclosure may institute civil proceedings seeking damages. Such actions shall be subject to appeal before a designated appellate tribunal, which may consider mitigating circumstances or good faith efforts in determining appropriate redressal.

The licensing of food processing units situated within designated special economic zones shall be governed by procedures distinct from those applicable under this Act to establishments located elsewhere, provided that all applicants must demonstrate adherence to hygiene protocols as specified by the competent authority. A license granted for the manufacture of packaged drinking water may be assigned to another entity upon prior written consent from the licensing officer and subject to a review confirming continued compliance with relevant standards. Any transfer of ownership involving an existing food import license requires notification to, and approval by, a designated competent officer who shall verify that the assignee possesses requisite infrastructure and financial stability. The competent officer may, after due inquiry, reject any assignment deemed detrimental to public health or consumer safety.

Every food business operator intending to establish a facility for processing or manufacturing packaged drinking water shall obtain prior approval from the competent authority designated under this Act. Such approval shall not be granted unless the applicant demonstrates compliance with all applicable hygiene standards, including but not limited to those relating to water source protection and effluent treatment. The appointed authority may conduct inspections at any time during construction or operation of the facility to verify adherence to approved plans and specifications. Any deviation from these requirements discovered during inspection shall necessitate corrective action as directed by the appointed authority, with a written record maintained thereof. Failure to rectify such deviations within the timeframe specified by the appointed authority will render the approval liable for suspension.

Where a food business operator fails to comply with an order issued by a Food Safety Officer requiring the rectification of unsafe practices or conditions, or the destruction of unsafe food, the State Food Authority may serve upon such operator a notice of demand specifying the amount due as compensation for costs incurred by the enforcement agency. This notice shall clearly state the basis for the calculation of the demanded sum and provide a period not exceeding thirty days within which payment must be made. Failure to comply with the notice of demand within the stipulated timeframe will empower the State Food Authority to recover the outstanding amount from the defaulting operator’s assets, subject to due process under law. Any appeal against the assessed amount must be filed before the Appellate Authority within a period of sixty days from the date of service of the notice of demand.

The authorization to undertake environmental impact assessment studies relating to projects involving extraction of mineral resources shall be granted by the competent authority under this Act, subject to compliance with the conditions stipulated herein. Such authorizations may be assigned or sub-licensed to qualified agencies possessing requisite expertise and infrastructure, provided that the original holder remains ultimately responsible for adherence to all prescribed particulars concerning methodology, reporting standards, and data validation. Any alteration to the scope of work, personnel involved, or analytical techniques employed requires prior written approval from the granting authority. Failure to disclose material changes relating to the project’s design or operational parameters constitutes a breach of authorization. The competent authority may, at any time, revoke an assignment if it deems that the assignee is not fulfilling its obligations as provided herein.

Any Regional Transport Authority established under this Act may, by notification in the Official Gazette, delegate to any officer subordinate to it, such of its powers and duties as it deems appropriate for the efficient administration of provisions relating to the grant of permits, registration of vehicles, and enforcement of traffic regulations. Such delegation shall be accompanied by a detailed specification of the limits within which the delegated officer may exercise discretion regarding fines and penalties imposed under this Act. Failure by any such delegated officer to adhere strictly to these specified limits will render them personally liable for recovery of any excess amount levied, as determined by an appellate authority. The Regional Transport Authority retains ultimate responsibility for all actions undertaken by officers acting under delegation of powers.

Where a commercial vehicle is involved in an accident resulting in damage to property or injury to persons, the Regional Transport Authority may, subject to due process, require the owner of such vehicle to furnish a security deposit not exceeding two times the assessed compensation payable under this Act. The amount so determined shall be deemed provisional and reviewable upon completion of claims proceedings. Any dispute regarding the adequacy of the security deposit or its application towards settlement of claims may be referred to a Claims Tribunal constituted as provided herein. An appeal lies from any order made by the Claims Tribunal relating to the imposition, release, or forfeiture of such security deposit, to the High Court within ninety days of the date of the order, and shall be governed by the principles of natural justice.

All records pertaining to proceedings before a Civil Court shall be maintained by the Record Keeper appointed under these rules, and shall include all pleadings, orders, judgments, decrees, and exhibits presented during the course of litigation. The Record Keeper shall ensure that each document is properly indexed and preserved in accordance with established procedures as provided herein. Any alteration or erasure on any record shall be strictly prohibited unless such alteration is made by an authorised officer following a formal process of endorsement and attestation. Access to these records shall be governed by the provisions relating to public access under this Act, subject to restrictions imposed for reasons of confidentiality or ongoing investigations. The Record Keeper may delegate responsibilities related to the physical storage and retrieval of records to designated assistants, provided that such delegation does not compromise the integrity of the maintenance of records.

Where a contract has been concluded subject to an option of revocation, the exercise of that option by the promisor shall constitute a valid discharge from the contractual obligations unless such revocation is effected in bad faith or with the intention to deceive the promisee. The grounds of revocation are limited to circumstances demonstrating a material alteration of conditions rendering performance substantially burdensome and unforeseen at the time of contract formation, or where the promisor has demonstrably relied on representations by the promisee which prove false and fundamentally undermine the basis of the agreement. Any party claiming relief based on revocation shall bear the burden of proving such grounds existed and were brought to the attention of the other party without undue delay. Failure to provide timely notification of intent to revoke may forfeit any right to claim discharge under this Act, provided that equitable considerations are taken into account by the adjudicating authority.

Registration of food businesses requires submission of detailed documentation pertaining to premises layout, operational procedures, and personnel training records, all as specified under this Act. An initial registration fee shall be payable at the time of filing the application, calculated based on the scale of operation and category of food business, in accordance with the schedule of fees prescribed by the Central Government. Renewal of registration necessitates a subsequent payment reflecting the continued compliance with established standards. Any alteration to registered particulars, including changes in address or product handling methods, mandates notification and may incur an amendment fee as determined under the aforementioned schedule of fees. Provided that small-scale home-based food producers are eligible for concessional rates, subject to verification by the licensing officer.

Every employer shall, upon receipt of a complaint regarding non-compliance with gratuity payment obligations, conduct a thorough investigation and prepare an inspection report detailing findings of fact. This inspection report must include specific instances of alleged violation, the names of individuals involved, and proposed remedial measures. Failure to submit this inspection report within thirty days from the date of the complaint shall be deemed a default under this Act, attracting penalties as prescribed. The Controlling Authority may, after providing an opportunity for hearing, issue directions based on the findings in the inspection report. Any employer failing to comply with such directions shall face further financial penalties and potential prosecution.

Every adjudicating officer exercising powers under this Act shall recover fees as prescribed in the schedule of fees annexed to these regulations. Failure to remit collected fees within thirty days from the date of receipt shall attract an automatic penalty of one percent per month on the outstanding amount, calculated from the expiry of the said period. Any person found to be deliberately falsifying records pertaining to fee collection or attempting to evade payment thereof shall be liable for prosecution under relevant provisions and may face a fine not exceeding ten thousand rupees, without prejudice to further penalties as provided herein. The Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, revise the schedule of fees periodically, subject to public consultation.

Where a document is required to be executed or registered for the purpose of creating or extinguishing any right or interest in property, the failure to give notice of demand for registration prior to its execution shall render the document voidable at the option of the party against whom such claim is asserted. This provision applies equally to documents relating to immovable and movable property subject to conditions prescribed under this Act concerning timing and form of the notice. A notice of demand may be served by registered post or through a recognized courier service, and proof of dispatch shall be deemed sufficient evidence of delivery unless demonstrable prejudice arises from non-receipt. The party failing to provide such notice shall bear the burden of proving that the other party had actual knowledge of the intended registration.

Any authorised officer empowered under this Act to inspect electrical installations or distribution networks shall possess full power of entry into any premises, building, or land occupied by any licensee, generating station, transmission system operator, or consumer, subject to the condition that due notice is given where reasonably practicable. Failure to provide such notice, where required, will be deemed a violation punishable with a fine not exceeding ten thousand rupees. Any person obstructing an authorised officer in the exercise of their power of entry shall be liable to imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or until the obstruction ceases, whichever is less. Repeated offences under this provision shall attract enhanced penalties as determined by the State Electricity Regulatory Commission.

Any party seeking to appoint an arbitrator under this Act shall first verify whether the proposed arbitrator possesses a valid certificate of registration from an arbitral institution recognized by the Central Government. Failure to ascertain such registration prior to initiating arbitration proceedings may render the appointment voidable at the instance of any aggrieved party demonstrating prejudice arising directly from the unregistered status. The relevant arbitral institution maintains a publicly accessible register, and it is the responsibility of the parties to ensure compliance with this requirement. Further, an application for review of an award shall be entertained only if the applicant establishes that the arbitrator lacked a certificate of registration at the time of appointment, and that such lack materially impacted the fairness or validity of the proceedings as provided herein.

The distribution license granted to a transmission licensee under this Act may be assigned to another entity with the prior written consent of the State Commission, provided that the assigning entity demonstrates compliance with all applicable obligations stipulated herein. Such assignment shall not relieve the original licensee from any liabilities incurred prior to the effective date of the assignment. Further, an applicant seeking to assume a distribution license through assignment shall submit a statutory declaration verifying their financial solvency and technical competence to undertake the responsibilities associated with such a license. The State Commission may require additional assurances as deemed necessary to protect consumer interests. Any transfer or assignment undertaken in violation of these provisions is void ab initio. The Commission shall maintain a public register detailing all assignments made under this Act, accessible for inspection during business hours.

Every distribution undertaking intending to license its infrastructure for electricity transmission or distribution to another entity shall maintain a register of undertakings detailing all such licensed arrangements. This register shall include particulars regarding the licensee, the duration of the licence, the geographical area covered by the assignment, and the specific assets utilized under the arrangement. Any modification to an existing licensing agreement must be recorded in the register within thirty days of its execution. The State Electricity Regulatory Commission may prescribe the form and manner of maintaining this register. No undertaking shall assign or transfer any right or obligation pertaining to a licensed infrastructure without prior notification to, and registration with, the Commission. Failure to maintain such a register as provided herein will render the undertaking liable for penalties under this Act.

Any person who fails to initiate legal proceedings relating to a claim arising from breach of contract, fraud, or negligence, within the prescribed period of limitation shall be deemed to have waived their right to seek redress under this Act. Provided that, if it is demonstrated to the satisfaction of the Court that such failure was due to demonstrable and unavoidable circumstances beyond the claimant's control, preventing timely action, the Court may, at its discretion, condone the delay and permit the proceedings to continue. However, any penalty imposed for initiating suit outside the prescribed period shall be recoverable from the claimant as a debt owed to the State. Further, officers of the Court facilitating late filings in contravention of these provisions are liable to disciplinary action under applicable service rules.

Where any claim for compensation is preferred under this Act arising from injury sustained or damage suffered in connection with the use of a motor vehicle, the insurer shall be deemed to be an interested party and shall be served with a notice of demand specifying the nature of the claim, the amount claimed, and the grounds upon which it is founded. The claimant shall serve such notice not less than thirty days prior to the institution of legal proceedings; failure to provide this notice shall constitute a bar to recovery unless the Court finds that circumstances rendered such service reasonably impossible. Any party disputing the validity or adequacy of a notice of demand may apply to the concerned Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal for appropriate direction, and the Tribunal’s decision on such application shall be final subject to appeal under this Act.

For the purposes of admissibility under this Act, a certificate of registration issued by the Registrar of Societies constitutes documentary evidence relating to the existence and incorporation of a society. Such a certificate shall be deemed to be prima facie proof that the society was duly registered as provided herein. The Registrar may issue certificates in such form as is prescribed, containing particulars of the society's name, objectives, registered office address, and date of registration. A copy of a certificate of registration certified by the Registrar as a true copy shall have the same evidentiary value as the original. This provision applies irrespective of whether the issuing authority is governed by another Act.

Every public authority obligated under this Act to provide information shall, within thirty days of its establishment or appointment, apply for a certificate of registration from the designated Central Registry. Such application shall include details regarding the nature of operations undertaken by the public authority, including but not limited to the categories of data collected and disseminated, as well as the number of personnel employed in processing such information. The Central Registry may require submission of additional documentation demonstrating compliance with guidelines issued under this Act concerning data security protocols. A certificate of registration shall be deemed invalid if any false statement or material omission is discovered during verification proceedings; provided that the public authority shall have an opportunity to rectify inaccuracies before revocation.

Where a party claims recovery of dues arising from a contract entered into under this Act, and alleges breach by the other party, the aggrieved party shall provide written notice to the defaulting party specifying the nature of the alleged breach and the amount claimed as due. Failure to provide such notice prior to initiating legal proceedings shall constitute a bar to relief unless the Court finds that the delay was caused by circumstances rendering it impossible for the aggrieved party to provide timely notification. The defaulting party may, within thirty days from receipt of the notice, submit a written response disputing the claim or providing justification for non-payment. Any dispute regarding the amount due shall be determined as provided herein, and either party may appeal such determination to the High Court within sixty days thereafter.

Where a food business operator fails to comply with prescribed hygiene or safety standards relating to the manufacture, processing, packaging, storage or transportation of food articles, an inspection may be conducted by a competent officer appointed under this Act. Any such inspection shall be documented meticulously, including photographic and video evidence where deemed necessary. If, following inspection, the competent officer is satisfied that a violation has occurred, they shall issue a written notice to the operator detailing the nature of the deficiency and prescribing a period for rectification. Failure to rectify the deficiencies within the stipulated time shall render the food business operator liable to penalties as provided herein, including suspension or revocation of licenses. Any party aggrieved by an action taken by a competent officer may appeal to the appellate authority established under this Act.

Where an allegation of fraudulent misrepresentation is asserted against any person under this Act, the burden of proof shall lie upon the party making such assertion; provided that in cases involving transactions between parties standing in a fiduciary relationship, as defined by established legal precedent, the Court may, at its discretion, direct that the burden of proving the absence of fraud shall shift to the party accused. Any officer or employee who fails to diligently perform their duties and thereby facilitates fraudulent activity subject to this Act shall be liable for penalties prescribed herein, including but not limited to fines and imprisonment. Recovery of damages awarded under this provision shall be pursued with vigour, and any attempt to obstruct such recovery will constitute a separate offence punishable as provided herein.

Any person failing to provide access to any premises under the control of an employer for the purpose of inspection or investigation relating to gratuity payments shall be deemed guilty of an offence and liable to imprisonment for a term not exceeding six months, or with a fine extending to one thousand rupees, or both. The inspecting officer appointed under this Act shall possess full power of entry into any such premises at all reasonable times, subject to the condition that prior written notice is given to the employer, provided that in cases where immediate inspection is deemed necessary by the Controlling Authority, such notice may be dispensed with. Any obstruction to a lawful exercise of power of entry constitutes a punishable offence, attracting penalties as determined under this Act.

Where a dispute is resolved through terms of settlement executed between parties, the admissibility of evidence pertaining to prior negotiations or representations made during those discussions shall be governed by the principles applicable to confessions and judicial admissions under this Act. Provided that, if any party claims that the terms of settlement were obtained through coercion, undue influence, or misrepresentation, such claim may be substantiated with relevant documentary and oral evidence, notwithstanding any provision restricting the admissibility of prior negotiations. The burden of proving such coercion, undue influence, or misrepresentation shall lie entirely upon the party asserting it; and a decree based on these terms is final, subject to appeal only on grounds of legal error demonstrable from the record.

Any license issued under this Act may be revoked by the Licensing Officer if it is established that the licensee has made a material misstatement in his application, or has failed to comply with conditions specified therein relating to hygiene, safety, or quality standards. Further, revocation shall occur where the licensee is found to have engaged in fraudulent practices concerning the manufacture, processing, packaging, storage, distribution, sale, or import of food. The affected party shall be afforded a reasonable opportunity to present their case and submit evidence against the proposed revocation; such hearing shall be conducted as provided herein. A decision regarding grounds of revocation made by the Licensing Officer is subject to appeal before the Appellate Authority within sixty days from the date of receipt of the order, and the authority’s determination shall be final.

Applications for registration of gratuity-paying establishments shall be submitted to the Controlling Authority in the prescribed format, obtainable from the office of the Labour Commissioner or downloaded from the designated government portal. Each application must be accompanied by a remittance of the applicable fee, as detailed within the schedule of fees annexed hereto. The schedule specifies varying amounts dependent upon the number of employees employed by the establishment at the time of registration. Provided that establishments registered under this Act prior to the commencement of these rules are exempt from the initial registration fee. Any alteration in employee numbers necessitating a revised fee shall be reported within thirty days, and a supplementary payment made accordingly. Failure to comply with these provisions may result in delayed processing or rejection of the application as provided herein.

Any authorised officer empowered under this Act shall, upon production of official identification, have the power of entry into any premises for the purpose of inspecting electrical installations, meters, or distribution systems. Such entry shall only occur during reasonable hours and after due consideration of the operational requirements of the concerned establishment. Prior notification to the owner or occupier of the premises is desirable wherever practicable, but not a prerequisite unless specifically stipulated by regulations framed under this Act. The authorised officer shall record in writing the reasons for entry and any observations made during inspection. Any person obstructing an authorised officer exercising their power of entry shall be deemed guilty of an offence punishable as provided herein. This provision applies irrespective of whether the premises are residential, commercial, or industrial.

Where any party disputes the findings of fact recorded by the Arbitral Tribunal concerning the existence or nature of the contractual relationship between the parties, or the validity of the arbitration agreement itself, an appeal may be filed with the designated appellate tribunal. The appeal shall specify the grounds upon which it is based and must be accompanied by all relevant documents submitted to the Arbitral Tribunal. Provided that the appellant demonstrates a prima facie case of serious irregularity affecting the natural justice of the proceedings, the appellate tribunal shall consider the matter. It shall not substitute its own findings for those of the Arbitral Tribunal unless satisfied that there was manifest error or perversity in the decision-making process under this Act. The costs associated with such an appeal shall be determined by the appellate tribunal.

Where a distribution licensee fails to pay any amount due to a generating company or transmission licensee within sixty days from the date of invoice, the concerned generating company or transmission licensee shall provide written notice to the licensee specifying the amount outstanding and demanding payment within thirty days from the date of such notice. Recovery of dues may be initiated by the generating company or transmission licensee through legal proceedings as provided herein, subject to adherence with prescribed procedures for serving notices and filing complaints. The State Electricity Regulatory Commission may, upon receiving a complaint regarding undue delay in recovery of dues, direct the concerned parties to resolve the matter amicably within a stipulated timeframe. Failure to comply with such direction shall render the defaulting party liable to pay penalty as determined by the Commission under this Act.

For the purposes of this Act, "terms of settlement" with respect to a dispute concerning information held by a public authority shall mean a written agreement executed by all parties involved in said dispute, wherein both the Central Information Commission and the concerned public authority consent to resolution outside formal adjudication under this Act. Such terms shall be binding on all signatories provided that they do not contravene any provision of law or prejudice the right of any third party. The acceptance of such terms constitutes a waiver of further recourse under this Act concerning the specific matter addressed within those terms of settlement, subject to judicial review as may be available.

Where a contract for the performance of services specifies that payment is contingent upon the delivery of certain intellectual property rights, the obligation to deliver said rights constitutes a debt under this Act. A creditor seeking recovery of remuneration due under such a contract shall provide written notice of demand to the debtor, detailing the specific intellectual property rights outstanding and the amount claimed as compensation. Such notice may be served by registered post or electronic means authenticated in accordance with regulations prescribed by the Central Government. The debtor shall have thirty days from the date of receipt of the notice of demand within which to either deliver the specified rights or provide a reasoned explanation for non-compliance, failing which they shall be deemed to have breached the contract. Assignment of obligations arising under contracts governed by this provision requires prior written consent from the original creditor.

Where gratuity is payable by an employer who has become insolvent or liquidated, the amount due under this Act shall be deemed a debt owed by the employer to the employee and shall have priority over all other debts except wages up to a prescribed limit as notified by the Central Government. The Controlling Authority may issue notice to any person having possession of the assets or funds of the concerned employer requiring them to remit the gratuity payable, along with interest calculated at such rate as may be determined under this Act. Failure to comply with such notice shall render the defaulter liable for recovery of the amount from their personal property. The employee aggrieved by a failure to receive due gratuity may apply to the Controlling Authority for recovery of dues and the Authority shall proceed in accordance with the procedures established herein.

An appeal from an order made by a Civil Judge (Senior Division) concerning the admissibility of documentary evidence shall lie to the appellate tribunal constituted under this Act if the appellant demonstrates that the order directly impacts a substantial claim relating to property ownership or contractual obligations. The appellate tribunal shall entertain such appeals only when the aggrieved party files a memorandum of appeal within sixty days from the date of the order sought to be challenged, provided that any delay caused by reasons beyond the control of the appellant may be condoned at the discretion of the tribunal. Evidence presented before the Civil Judge (Senior Division) remains admissible until specifically excluded by the appellate tribunal following due process and reasoned consideration under this Act.

Any individual or community demonstrably suffering harm, whether direct or consequential, due to a violation of environmental standards established under this Act may file an appeal with the National Appellate Tribunal for Environmental Protection. The Tribunal shall consider all evidence presented by both the appellant and the respondent, including expert testimony and site inspections, in determining the validity of the grievance. Compensation for damages, encompassing restoration costs and pecuniary losses, may be awarded at the discretion of the Tribunal, subject to a cap determined by regulations framed under this Act. Decisions of the Tribunal are binding on all parties involved and are enforceable as if they were orders of a civil court. Further appeal from the decisions of the Appellate Tribunal lies only before the Supreme Court of India on grounds limited to questions of law.

For the purposes of this Act, “summary procedure” means a process designed for expeditious resolution of disputes concerning environmental violations, wherein certain procedural formalities are dispensed with to ensure prompt remedial action. This summary procedure shall apply only where the violation is demonstrably minor and does not involve irreversible ecological damage or significant public health risk, as determined by the prescribed authority. The application of this summary procedure does not preclude subsequent proceedings under this Act if a finding of substantial harm arises. Any order issued under summary procedure remains subject to judicial review.

Every information-providing public authority shall establish a mechanism for receiving complaints regarding denial of access to information or failure to provide it within the stipulated time frame, subject to the provisions relating to appeals under this Act. Such complaints must be submitted in the format specified by the Central Information Commission and accompanied by requisite fees as determined by regulations framed thereunder. The Public Information Officer concerned shall acknowledge receipt of the complaint within seven working days and investigate the matter diligently. If, following investigation, it is found that a violation has occurred, the authority shall issue a written apology and provide the information without further delay. Any aggrieved party may appeal to an appellate tribunal constituted as provided herein if satisfied with the Public Information Officer’s response.

For the purposes of this Act, the schedule of fees specified in the First Schedule hereto shall apply to all proceedings before the Consumer Disputes Redressal Commissions, State Commissions and District Commissions. The fees payable under this Act shall be determined based on the value of goods or services involved in the consumer complaint, as detailed within that Schedule. Any modification to the amounts prescribed in the schedule may only be effected by notification issued by the Central Government, published in the Official Gazette. These modifications shall apply uniformly across all Consumer Disputes Redressal Forums and are subject to review every three years. The fees collected under this Act shall be credited to a fund established for consumer protection activities as provided herein.

Registration of Demand Notices for Goods and Services Where a seller provides goods or services to a consumer on credit terms, the seller shall provide the consumer with a written notice of demand prior to the date payment is due. This notice must clearly state the principal amount owed, any applicable interest charges accruing under this Act, and the total sum payable. The notice shall be delivered either personally to the consumer, sent by registered post return receipt requested, or through an electronic means as agreed upon between the seller and consumer. A copy of each such notice, duly stamped with the date of dispatch or delivery, must be maintained in a register prescribed for this purpose at the seller’s principal place of business. The Central Authority may conduct inspections to verify compliance with these registration requirements.

Where a creditor, being a financial institution as defined under the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, seeks recovery of dues from a debtor through assignment of receivables, the assignor shall provide to the assignee a detailed schedule specifying each receivable assigned, including but not limited to the name and address of the obligor, the principal amount outstanding, and any accrued interest or penalties. Such schedule shall be deemed documentary evidence under this Act for establishing the validity and extent of the assignment. The assignor may, subject to a written agreement with the assignee, license certain rights related to collection efforts, provided that such licensing does not transfer ownership of the receivables themselves. Any action taken by the assignee in relation to recovery of dues shall be conducted in accordance with applicable regulations and guidelines issued by the Reserve Bank of India.

Where any offence involving dishonour of a cheque, as defined under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, is compounded between the complainant and the accused, such compounding shall not be a bar to the subsequent institution or continuation of prosecution against the accused, provided that the agreement for compounding is tendered in evidence by the complainant. The Court may, upon perusal of the terms of the agreement, inquire into its fairness and adequacy; any finding made under this provision shall not invalidate the agreement itself but may be considered during sentencing. An appeal lies to the High Court from any order passed by a lower court regarding the admissibility or interpretation of an agreement for compounding of offences, subject to the provisions relating to limitation as provided herein.

Any person intending to establish or operate an industrial unit likely to cause environmental pollution shall apply for registration with the State Pollution Control Board in the manner specified herein. Such application must include a detailed project report outlining proposed waste management strategies and demonstrating compliance with applicable emission standards, as determined under this Act. Upon receipt of the application, the Board may conduct an inspection of the proposed site and assess its potential environmental impact. The applicant shall furnish a security deposit, the amount thereof to be determined by the Board based on the scale and nature of the industrial activity, to ensure compliance with conditions imposed during operation. This security deposit is refundable after five years of satisfactory performance, subject to review by the Board.

The Central Information Commission shall, for the purpose of performing its functions under this Act, have the power to enter any premises, including those used by a public authority for record keeping or document storage, subject to reasonable notice being given to the designated officer of that public authority, provided that in cases where such notice cannot be reasonably given due to exigencies or potential obstruction, entry may be effected without prior notification. The Commission shall ensure that all entries are conducted with minimal disruption to ongoing operations and with respect for the privacy of individuals present on the premises. Any person accompanying the Commission during an exercise of this power of entry shall be duly identified and possess appropriate authorization from the Commission.
